\textbf{Parameter Type} & \texttt{param\_\allowbreak{}type} &  &  & O/F Ratio \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Parameter to vary during sweep analysis. O/F Ratio: optimize mixture ratio for performance. Chamber Pressure: study pressure effects. Expansion Ratio: optimize nozzle design. Altitude: analyze altitude performance. Options: O/F Ratio; Chamber Pressure; Expansion Ratio; Altitude.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Start Value} & \texttt{param\_\allowbreak{}start} &  &  & 1.5 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} First value of the sweep (in the unit of the swept parameter). The sweep runs from this value to the end value and includes both ends; the two ends are computed first, so a sweep cut short by the time budget still spans the whole range. For an O/F sweep, an untouched range is set to 50-150 \% of the design O/F (HRMA choice, so the design point and the propellant's Isp peak lie inside).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{End Value} & \texttt{param\_\allowbreak{}end} &  &  & 4.0 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Last value of the sweep (in the unit of the swept parameter); it is always computed. For an O/F sweep, an untouched range is set to 50-150 \% of the design O/F (HRMA choice).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Number of Steps} & \texttt{param\_\allowbreak{}steps} &  & 3 -- 50 & 10 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Number of calculation points between start and end values. More steps provide smoother curves but require more computation time.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{calculate\_trajectory} & \texttt{calculate\_\allowbreak{}trajectory} &  &  & checked \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Whether Calculate also flies the trajectory (sent as calculate\_trajectory). Checked: after the motor is solved, the flight is integrated with the motor result and the vehicle and launch inputs on this tab. Unchecked: the result carries no trajectory; it is reported as a skipped step with no flight numbers. Default: checked (the server default is also true). Accepted: true or false; any other value is refused by name.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Initial Altitude} & \texttt{traj\_\allowbreak{}alt\_\allowbreak{}start} & m & 0 -- 50000 & 0 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Starting altitude of the trajectory (m), sent as trajectory\_start\_altitude; the trajectory endpoint accepts the ISA table range and starts the flight there. \emph{If blank:} Empty or not a number: the trajectory is not computed and the field is named (no altitude is assumed).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Final Altitude} & \texttt{traj\_\allowbreak{}alt\_\allowbreak{}end} & m & 0 -- 100000 & 10000 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Upper altitude of the analysis (m). Informational: /api/trajectory-analysis does NOT read it (measured: the result is identical with or without it; the endpoint names it under inputs\_not\_read). The flight is integrated through apogee to landing. \emph{If blank:} Empty: not sent.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Analysis Points} & \texttt{traj\_\allowbreak{}points} &  & 5 -- 100 & 20 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Number of output points along the trajectory. Informational: /api/trajectory-analysis does NOT read it (measured: the result is identical with or without it; the endpoint names it under inputs\_not\_read); the solver uses its own step. \emph{If blank:} Empty: not sent.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Initial Mass} & \texttt{initial\_\allowbreak{}mass} & kg & 1 -- 10000 & 50 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Total vehicle mass at ignition including propellant, structure, and payload.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Final Mass} & \texttt{final\_\allowbreak{}mass} & kg & 1 -- 10000 & 25 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Vehicle mass after propellant consumption (dry mass + payload).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Drag Coefficient} & \texttt{drag\_\allowbreak{}coefficient} &  & 0.1 -- 2.0 & 0.5 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Aerodynamic drag coefficient.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Reference Area} & \texttt{reference\_\allowbreak{}area} & mm\textsuperscript{2} & 100 -- 10000000 & 17671 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Cross-sectional area used for drag calculations. Entered in square millimetres and converted to square metres before it is sent to the solver.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Launch Angle} & \texttt{launch\_\allowbreak{}angle} & degrees & 0 -- 90 & 90 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Launch angle from the horizontal (degrees), sent as launch\_angle: 90\ensuremath{^\circ} = vertical launch, 45\ensuremath{^\circ} = maximum-range trajectory; the endpoint accepts 0--90. \emph{If blank:} Empty or not a number: the trajectory is not computed and the field is named (no angle is assumed).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Wind Speed} & \texttt{wind\_\allowbreak{}speed} & m/s & 0 -- 50 & 0 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Horizontal wind speed affecting the trajectory (m/s), sent as wind\_speed; must be \ensuremath{\ge} 0 and below the ISA sea-level speed of sound. \emph{If blank:} Empty or not a number: the trajectory is not computed and the field is named (no wind is assumed).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Launch Altitude} & \texttt{launch\_\allowbreak{}altitude} & m & 0 -- 6000 & 0 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Elevation of the launch site above sea level. Sets the starting altitude and the ambient conditions the trajectory begins from.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Wind Direction} & \texttt{wind\_\allowbreak{}direction} & degrees & 0 -- 360 & 0 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Compass direction the wind blows towards, measured clockwise from the launch azimuth. 0\ensuremath{^\circ} = tailwind along the launch heading.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Parachute Area} & \texttt{parachute\_\allowbreak{}area} & m2 & \ensuremath{\ge}\,0 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Projected (canopy) area of the recovery parachute. Descent velocity scales as 1/sqrt(area). \emph{If blank:} Leave empty to keep the solver assumption, which is reported as an assumption in the results.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Parachute Cd} & \texttt{parachute\_\allowbreak{}cd} &  & \ensuremath{\ge}\,0 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Drag coefficient of the parachute referenced to its projected area (1.4 is the classic flat-circular value). \emph{If blank:} Leave empty to keep the solver assumption.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Deploy Delay after Apogee} & \texttt{parachute\_\allowbreak{}deploy\_\allowbreak{}delay} & s & \ensuremath{\ge}\,0 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Time between apogee and canopy inflation. The vehicle falls ballistically during this delay. \emph{If blank:} Leave empty to keep the solver assumption.} \\ \midrule
\end{longtable}}

It must be at least grain length plus pre-combustion chamber length; a shorter value is not applied, the automatic length is used and the warning gives the minimum. \emph{If blank:} Empty or 0: the length is derived from L* (automatic).} \\ \midrule

\textbf{Include Cooling Channels} & \texttt{cooling\_\allowbreak{}channels} &  &  & None \\*

\textbf{Ambient Temperature, $T_a$} & \texttt{ambient\_\allowbreak{}temp} & K & 180 -- 340 & (blank) \\*

Wall zones & -- & Three-zone wall verdict, liner thickness. & Table~\ref{tab:u1-cidar}. \\
Blank-field assumptions & -- & Values used for fields left empty. & The server's declaration list. \\
Charts & -- & Regression rate and port growth, motor cross-section, performance dashboard, thrust and chamber pressure vs time, injector schematic, altitude performance, total impulse vs altitude, combustion products through the nozzle, combustion analysis, operating-point dashboard. & Time-stepped solution and equilibrium calculation. \\
Side panels & -- & Transient Analysis, Tank Blowdown, Structural FEA, Thermal FEA, Flight Dynamics (6-DOF), Injector Design. & Tables~\ref{tab:y-zaman}--\ref{tab:y-fea-t}. \\
\ui{NASA CEA Comparison} & -- & HRMA equilibrium and RocketCEA (NASA CEA) at the same operating point. & Section~\ref{sec:cea}. \\
\end{longtable}

\subsection{Limits}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em]
  \item The regression law is of the form $r = a\,G^n$; scale effects,
  combustion instability and ignition transients are not modelled.
  \item In user tank-pressure mode, regulator lock-up and thermal drift of the
  tank are not modelled; the tank structural mass is not computed.
  \item H\textsubscript{2}O\textsubscript{2} in the hybrid is taken as 100\,\% pure.
\end{itemize}

\section{Solid Motor Page}\label{sec:kati}

\subsection{Purpose}

Computes the burning area from the grain geometry, the internal ballistics
(chamber pressure, thrust curve), the nozzle, the case and closure thickness
and the mass breakdown of a solid propellant motor.

\subsection{Screen}

\ekran{img/v3_0_5/kati_form_yakit_en.png}{Solid page: \ui{1. PROPELLANT
PROPERTIES}. Note the \ui{Thermochemistry source} selector and the fields
that open with the grain type.}{fig:kati-form}

\subsection{Inputs}

The default of an empty solid page is KNDX propellant with three BATES grains
(outer diameter 100~mm, core 48~mm, total length 400~mm). With
\ui{Thermochemistry source (T\_c, M, $\gamma$, c*)} set to \ui{Catalogue
record} the flame temperature, molar mass, $\gamma$ and $c^*$ boxes are
read-only and not sent; the solver takes these values from NASA CEA at the
motor's chamber pressure and, after the calculation, writes the value used
below each box. With \ui{My value} the four boxes are sent and the run is
declared as user input.

\ekran{img/v3_0_5/kati_yakit_katalogu_en.png}{\ui{0. PROPELLANT CATALOGUE}:
family filter, records and the source column of each record.}{fig:kati-katalog}

CASING}: case material, yield-strength source, wall, liner and

It sets the propellant mass of the grain, so the burn time, total impulse and the mass flow that sizes the throat change with it. Picking a catalogue record fills it with the record value (see the catalogue row); the value you type here is sent and used. Accepted range 500-3000 kg/m\textsuperscript{3}. \emph{If blank:} The selected record's density is used.} \\ \midrule

The catalogue has no \ensuremath{\Delta}Hc for any propellant, so picking a record clears this box unless you typed your own value. The box accepts 500-10000 kJ/kg; the solver does not use it. \emph{If blank:} Nothing is sent and no result changes.} \\ \midrule

"Catalogue record" (default): the four boxes below show the selected record's values at ONE reference pressure, are read-only and are NOT sent; for a propellant with a known composition the solver computes them with NASA CEA at the motor chamber pressure (otherwise it uses the record values and says so in the warnings), and after Calculate each box shows the value the solver used underneath. "My values": the four boxes are sent and replace the thermochemistry; NASA CEA is then not applied and the result reports the source as user\_entered. Options: Catalogue record - solver uses NASA CEA at motor Pc; My value. \emph{If blank:} A blank box in "My values" is not sent (the record value is used for it).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Adiabatic Flame Temperature Tc, $T_c$} & \texttt{flame\_\allowbreak{}temp} & K &  & 1713.1 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Adiabatic flame (chamber) temperature T\_c in K. It sets the gas enthalpy behind c* and Isp and the throat heat flux. "Catalogue record" mode: shows the selected record's value at one pressure (see the catalogue row) and is not sent; the value the solver used (NASA CEA at the motor chamber pressure) appears below after Calculate. "My values" mode: this number is sent and used. Accepted range 1000-4500 K.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Molecular Weight M, $\mathcal{M}$} & \texttt{molecular\_\allowbreak{}weight} & g/mol &  & 37.51 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Mean molar mass M of the combustion products in g/mol (= kg/kmol). It enters c* and Isp (lower M gives higher values) and the gas properties of the heat-flux model. "Catalogue record" mode: shows the selected record's value at one pressure and is not sent; the solver's value (NASA CEA at the motor chamber pressure, mixture mass per mole of gas, condensed phase included) appears below after Calculate - it can differ from the catalogue value because the catalogue rows use different molar conventions. "My values" mode: this number is sent and used. Accepted range 2-100 g/mol.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Specific Heat Ratio \ensuremath{\gamma}, $\gamma$} & \texttt{gamma} &  & 1.05 -- 1.5 & 1.122 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Ratio of specific heats \ensuremath{\gamma} = Cp/Cv of the chamber gas. It enters c* and the nozzle expansion (exit pressure, thrust coefficient). "Catalogue record" mode: shows the selected record's value at one pressure and is not sent; the solver's value (NASA CEA at the motor chamber pressure, shifting equilibrium) appears below after Calculate. "My values" mode: this number is sent and used. Accepted range 1.05-1.5.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Characteristic Velocity c*, $c^*$} & \texttt{char\_\allowbreak{}velocity} & m/s & 700 -- 2500 & 915.9 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Theoretical characteristic velocity c* in m/s, before the combustion efficiency. It sizes the throat (A\_t = \ensuremath{\dot m}\ensuremath{\cdot}c*/Pc) and the thrust. "Catalogue record" mode: shows the selected record's value at one pressure (see the catalogue row) and is not sent; the solver's value (NASA CEA at the motor chamber pressure) appears below after Calculate. "My values" mode: this number is sent and replaces the thermochemistry (NASA CEA is not applied). "Calculate" computes c* from \ensuremath{\gamma}, T\_c and M (Sutton \& Biblarz Eq. 3-32) and switches the source to "My values". Accepted range 700-2500 m/s; outside it the value is ignored with a warning.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Erosive Burning Coefficient k} & \texttt{erosive\_\allowbreak{}k\_\allowbreak{}source} &  &  & Catalogue (propellant record) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Erosive burning coefficient k of the mass-flux law (dimensionless here; the solver multiplies the base rate by 1 + k\ensuremath{\cdot}(G/G\_ref)\textasciicircum{}m with m from the field below). It raises the burn rate where the port gas mass flux G is high, so it changes the start of the thrust curve, the peak pressure and the burn time. Source selector: "Catalogue" uses the value calibrated in the propellant record (this box is then read-only and shows the value the solver used after Calculate); "My value" sends this number and the solver applies it. Accepted range 0-1. Options: Catalogue (propellant record); My value. \emph{If blank:} In "My value" mode: nothing is sent and the catalogue value is used.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Erosive Burning Coefficient k, $k_e$} & \texttt{erosive\_\allowbreak{}k} &  & 0 -- 1 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Erosive burning coefficient k of the mass-flux law (dimensionless here; the solver multiplies the base rate by 1 + k\ensuremath{\cdot}(G/G\_ref)\textasciicircum{}m with m from the field below). It raises the burn rate where the port gas mass flux G is high, so it changes the start of the thrust curve, the peak pressure and the burn time. Source selector: "Catalogue" uses the value calibrated in the propellant record (this box is then read-only and shows the value the solver used after Calculate); "My value" sends this number and the solver applies it. Accepted range 0-1. \emph{If blank:} In "My value" mode: nothing is sent and the catalogue value is used.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Erosive Burning Exponent m} & \texttt{erosive\_\allowbreak{}m} &  & 0.1 -- 2 & 0.8 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Exponent for erosive burning law. Higher values indicate stronger dependence on mass flux.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Temperature Coefficient \ensuremath{\sigma}} & \texttt{temp\_\allowbreak{}coeff\_\allowbreak{}source} & 1/K &  & Catalogue (propellant record) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Temperature sensitivity \ensuremath{\sigma}p of the burn rate (1/K). The solver uses the exponential law a\_T = a\ensuremath{\cdot}exp(\ensuremath{\sigma}p\ensuremath{\cdot}(T0 \ensuremath{-} T\_ref)), where T0 is the grain temperature (Initial Temperature field) and T\_ref the record reference temperature; it shifts the burn rate, so chamber pressure, thrust and burn time change when T0 \ensuremath{\neq} T\_ref. It also sets the cold/hot-day sensitivity table. Source selector: "Catalogue" uses the propellant record value (read-only box, filled after Calculate); "My value" sends this number. Accepted range 0-0.02 1/K. Options: Catalogue (propellant record); My value. \emph{If blank:} In "My value" mode: nothing is sent and the catalogue value is used.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Temperature Coefficient \ensuremath{\sigma}, $\sigma_p$} & \texttt{temp\_\allowbreak{}coeff} & 1/K & 0 -- 0.02 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Temperature sensitivity \ensuremath{\sigma}p of the burn rate (1/K). The solver uses the exponential law a\_T = a\ensuremath{\cdot}exp(\ensuremath{\sigma}p\ensuremath{\cdot}(T0 \ensuremath{-} T\_ref)), where T0 is the grain temperature (Initial Temperature field) and T\_ref the record reference temperature; it shifts the burn rate, so chamber pressure, thrust and burn time change when T0 \ensuremath{\neq} T\_ref. It also sets the cold/hot-day sensitivity table. Source selector: "Catalogue" uses the propellant record value (read-only box, filled after Calculate); "My value" sends this number. Accepted range 0-0.02 1/K. \emph{If blank:} In "My value" mode: nothing is sent and the catalogue value is used.} \\ \midrule
\end{longtable}}

\textbf{Number of Grains N, $N$} & \texttt{grain\_\allowbreak{}count} &  & \ensuremath{\ge}\,1 & 3 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Total number of propellant grains in the motor. Multiple grains reduce manufacturing stress and allow for modular design.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Web Thickness, $w$} & \texttt{web\_\allowbreak{}thickness} & mm &  & 26.0 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Derived output, read-only: the propellant web implied by the grain geometry ((outer \ensuremath{-} core)/2), filled after Calculate. When the outer surface burns as well the web is consumed from both faces, so the thickness actually burnt is half of it (see web\_burnout\_mm). Typing here changes no result.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Grain Type} & \texttt{grain\_\allowbreak{}type} &  &  & BATES (Cylindrical) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Geometric configuration of the solid propellant grain. BATES: cylinder with a central core port. Star: star-shaped core port. Finocyl: core port with fins for a larger burning surface. Wagon Wheel: multiple core ports. End Burner: no core port, burns from one end only. The thrust profile is NOT fixed by the shape alone (it also depends on the inhibitor layout and the port-to-throat ratio); this run's profile is classified by the solver and printed under "Thrust Curve". Options: BATES (Cylindrical); Star; Finocyl; Slotted; Wagon Wheel; End Burner.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Grain Support} & \texttt{grain\_\allowbreak{}support} &  &  & Case-bonded \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} How the grain is held in the case. Case-bonded: cast and cured inside the case and bonded to its liner; the case restrains the cure and cool-down shrinkage, so the bore carries that thermal strain on top of the pressure strain. Cartridge-loaded: cast in a mold or liner outside the case and inserted, bonded at most at its ends (NASA SP-8073); no shrinkage strain is restrained, and the pressure strain is computed with the case supporting the grain (snug fit, upper bound). Changes only the grain structural results (bore strain, strain safety factor, crack risk), not the ballistics. If the field is not sent, case-bonded is used and declared in the result. Options: Case-bonded; Cartridge-loaded (free-standing).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Outer Diameter, $D_g$} & \texttt{outer\_\allowbreak{}diameter} & mm &  & 100 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Outer diameter of the propellant grain. Must be smaller than chamber inner diameter to allow for insulation and clearance.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Core Diameter, $d_c$} & \texttt{core\_\allowbreak{}diameter} & mm &  & 48 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Initial diameter of the central core hole (port diameter). Determines initial burning surface area and thrust profile. Measured in this solver for a BATES grain with burning ends (10-60 mm cores): the end plateau is below the start plateau at every core (end/start 0.09-0.49) and a larger core falls off less, but the trend is not monotonic (0.11 at 10 mm, 0.09 at 15 mm, 0.21 at 30 mm, 0.49 at 60 mm). At 10 mm the solver classifies the curve as Progressive-Regressive (thrust rises first, then falls), so this is not a single class over the whole core range. The published shape class comes from thrust\_profile\_analysis.thrust\_curve\_type in the result, not from this hint.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Grain Length, $L_g$} & \texttt{grain\_\allowbreak{}length} & mm &  & 400 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Total axial length of the propellant stack, not of a single segment. The solver splits this length across the segment count (each BATES segment is L / N long), so changing the segment count does not change the propellant mass. Longer stacks provide more total impulse but may cause combustion instability.} \\ \midrule
\end{longtable}}

\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Radius of fillets at star valleys to reduce stress concentration. Improves grain structural integrity.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Number of Fins} & \texttt{fin\_\allowbreak{}count} &  & \ensuremath{\ge}\,2 & 4 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Number of radial fins extending from core. More fins provide higher burning surface area.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Fin Width} & \texttt{fin\_\allowbreak{}width} & mm &  & 8 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Thickness of each fin slot. Affects burning surface area and grain structural integrity.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Fin Length} & \texttt{fin\_\allowbreak{}length} & mm & 1 -- 200 & 20 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Radial length of fin slots from core to outer diameter. Determines progressive burning characteristics.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Finned Length Fraction} & \texttt{finned\_\allowbreak{}length\_\allowbreak{}fraction} &  & 0.05 -- 1 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Fraction of the grain length that carries the fins (dimensionless, 0.05-1); the rest of the grain is a plain cylindrical port. A larger fraction raises the initial burning area, so thrust at start-up and the curve shape change. Accepted range 0.05-1. \emph{If blank:} Nothing is sent and the solver applies 0.4 (HRMA default, declared in the result under "The solver assumed these inputs").} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Number of Outer Holes} & \texttt{wagon\_\allowbreak{}hole\_\allowbreak{}count} &  & 3 -- 12 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Number of outer port holes around the central hole (whole number). More holes raise the initial burning area and the start-up thrust. Accepted range 3-12; holes that would intersect are rejected with the largest usable hole diameter. \emph{If blank:} The solver uses 6 (HRMA selection, declared in the result).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Hole Diameter} & \texttt{wagon\_\allowbreak{}hole\_\allowbreak{}diameter} & mm & \ensuremath{\ge}\,0.1 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Diameter of every port hole, the central one and the outer ones (mm). It sets the initial port area and burning perimeter, so it changes the port-to-throat ratio, the start-up thrust and the burn time. Accepted: above 0.1 mm and below the limit where holes touch each other or the grain surface (the rejection names that limit). \emph{If blank:} Core diameter / 2 (HRMA selection, declared in the result).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Pitch Circle Diameter} & \texttt{wagon\_\allowbreak{}pitch\_\allowbreak{}diameter} & mm & \ensuremath{\ge}\,0.1 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Diameter of the circle through the centres of the outer holes (mm). It sets how far the outer holes sit from the central hole and from the grain surface, so it changes when the webs between holes burn through. Accepted: 0.1 mm up to the grain outer diameter, with no hole intersecting another or the grain surface. \emph{If blank:} Grain outer diameter / 2 (HRMA selection, declared in the result).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Number of Slots} & \texttt{slot\_\allowbreak{}count} &  & 2 -- 24 & 6 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Number of longitudinal slots cut radially from the central port. More slots raise the initial burning area.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Slot Width} & \texttt{slot\_\allowbreak{}width} & mm & \ensuremath{\ge}\,0.5 & 4 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Circumferential thickness of each slot. Wider slots burn out sooner and shift the curve towards regressive.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Slot Depth} & \texttt{slot\_\allowbreak{}depth} & mm & \ensuremath{\ge}\,1 & 20 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Radial depth measured from the port wall. Deep slots reach the case early and make the curve regressive; shallow slots stay progressive. Must remain inside the available web.} \\ \midrule
\end{longtable}}

\textbf{inhibit\_front} & \texttt{inhibit\_\allowbreak{}front} &  &  & unchecked \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Prevents burning on the forward end face. In a BATES stack the end faces are left EXPOSED: the growing core area offsets the shrinking end area, and the burn is neutral when each grain is (3D + d)/2 long (D outer, d core diameter; burn area at burnout equals burn area at ignition). Measured at 100/48 mm, 3 × 174 mm: Kn 222.7 -\textgreater{} 223.4, peak +8.3\%. The default grain (3 × 133.3 mm) is shorter and burns regressive: Kn 235.0 -\textgreater{} 187.9 (-20.0\%). With the outer surface inhibited, coating both ends makes the burn area grow (default grain: Kn 214.0 -\textgreater{} 236.0, peak +13.4\%) -- tick this only if you want that.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{inhibit\_rear} & \texttt{inhibit\_\allowbreak{}rear} &  &  & unchecked \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Prevents burning on the aft end face. In a BATES stack the end faces are left EXPOSED: the growing core area offsets the shrinking end area, and the burn is neutral when each grain is (3D + d)/2 long (D outer, d core diameter; burn area at burnout equals burn area at ignition). Measured at 100/48 mm, 3 × 174 mm: Kn 222.7 -\textgreater{} 223.4, peak +8.3\%. The default grain (3 × 133.3 mm) is shorter and burns regressive: Kn 235.0 -\textgreater{} 187.9 (-20.0\%). With the outer surface inhibited, coating both ends makes the burn area grow (default grain: Kn 214.0 -\textgreater{} 236.0, peak +13.4\%) -- tick this only if you want that.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{inhibit\_outer} & \texttt{inhibit\_\allowbreak{}outer} &  &  & checked \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Prevents burning on outer cylindrical surface.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Grain-to-Grain Gap} & \texttt{grain\_\allowbreak{}gap} & mm &  & 2 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Spacing between individual grains. Allows for thermal expansion and prevents grain-to-grain bonding during storage.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Insulation Thickness, $t_{ins}$} & \texttt{insulation\_\allowbreak{}thickness} & mm & 0 -- 100 & 3 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Thickness of thermal insulation layer between propellant and case. Protects case from high temperatures and provides thermal barrier.} \\ \midrule
\end{longtable}}

\textbf{Structural material catalogue - apply to} & \texttt{material\_\allowbreak{}catalog\_\allowbreak{}target} &  &  & Case / chamber \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Options: Case / chamber; Nozzle.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Chamber Diameter, $D_c$} & \texttt{chamber\_\allowbreak{}diameter} & mm &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Case inner diameter in mm - the bore that holds the grain, liner and insulation (the grain outer diameter is its own field). It sizes the case wall, the case mass and the burst margin. A value below that minimum is rejected with the minimum named; the case is never enlarged silently. Accepted range 10-5000 mm. \emph{If blank:} Derived as grain outer diameter + 2\ensuremath{\cdot}(liner + insulation) and shown after Calculate.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Case Internal Volume} & \texttt{chamber\_\allowbreak{}volume} & L & 0.01 -- 16000 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Your stated free volume inside the case (case bore minus propellant), in litres. The solver derives this volume from the geometry and uses its own value; the number you type is only compared with it and a named warning appears when they disagree (measured: changing it changes only the warnings, not thrust, pressure or burn time). Accepted range 0.001-100000 L. \emph{If blank:} (default): nothing is sent and no comparison is made.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Case Material} & \texttt{case\_\allowbreak{}material} &  &  & Carbon steel (generic, A36-class) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Material of the motor case. The case wall is sized against hoop stress with this material's yield strength (see the yield source below), the case and closure mass come from its density, and the case thermal verdict compares the computed case wall temperature with its service temperature limit (shown below the selection; where no limit is on record the verdict is not evaluated). Options come from the server material records; a name the server cannot resolve is rejected. Options: AISI 4130 low-alloy steel (normalized); Carbon steel (generic, A36-class); Stainless steel 304 (annealed); Stainless steel 316 (annealed); Aluminum 6061-T6; Titanium Ti-6Al-4V; Inconel 718 (aged); Aluminum 7075-T6; Aluminum 2024-T3; Stainless 17-4PH (H900); AISI 4340 low-alloy steel (normalized); Inconel 625 (annealed); Titanium CP Grade 2; Magnesium AZ31B-H24; Filament-wound composite (generic).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Yield Strength \ensuremath{\sigma}y} & \texttt{yield\_\allowbreak{}strength\_\allowbreak{}source} & MPa &  & From material \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Yield strength \ensuremath{\sigma}y of the case material (MPa). It sizes the case wall (hoop stress with the safety factor) and sets the burst pressure and the burst margin. Source selector: "From material" uses the yield of the selected case material record for BOTH the wall sizing and the burst pressure (this box is then read-only and shows that value); "My value" sends this number, which sizes the wall, while the burst pressure still comes from the material record (a named warning says so when the two differ). Accepted range 10-3000 MPa. Options: From material; My value. \emph{If blank:} In "My value" mode: nothing is sent and the material record is used.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Yield Strength \ensuremath{\sigma}y, $\sigma_y$} & \texttt{yield\_\allowbreak{}strength} & MPa & 10 -- 3000 & 250 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Yield strength \ensuremath{\sigma}y of the case material (MPa). It sizes the case wall (hoop stress with the safety factor) and sets the burst pressure and the burst margin. Source selector: "From material" uses the yield of the selected case material record for BOTH the wall sizing and the burst pressure (this box is then read-only and shows that value); "My value" sends this number, which sizes the wall, while the burst pressure still comes from the material record (a named warning says so when the two differ). Accepted range 10-3000 MPa. \emph{If blank:} In "My value" mode: nothing is sent and the material record is used.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Safety Factor FoS, FoS} & \texttt{safety\_\allowbreak{}factor} &  & 1.1 -- 10 & 2.5 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Factor of safety for case design. Higher values provide more safety margin but increase case weight. Required by safety codes for amateur rocketry.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Liner Thickness, $t_{lin}$} & \texttt{liner\_\allowbreak{}thickness} & mm & 0.1 -- 100 & 2 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Thickness of insulating liner layer. Protects case from hot combustion gases and provides thermal barrier.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Liner Density} & \texttt{liner\_\allowbreak{}density} & kg/m\textsuperscript{3} & 200 -- 3000 & 1200 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Density of liner material for mass calculation. Phenolic: 1200-1400 kg/m\textsuperscript{3}, EPDM: 1200-1300 kg/m\textsuperscript{3}. Affects overall motor mass.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Initial Temperature, $T_0$} & \texttt{initial\_\allowbreak{}temp} & K & 200 -- 350 & 298 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Grain (propellant conditioning) temperature T0 at ignition, in K - not the chamber gas temperature. The burn rate is shifted with the exponential law a\_T = a\ensuremath{\cdot}exp(\ensuremath{\sigma}p\ensuremath{\cdot}(T0 \ensuremath{-} T\_ref)) (\ensuremath{\sigma}p: Temperature Coefficient field, T\_ref: the record reference temperature), so chamber pressure, thrust, burn time and Isp change with it (measured on the KNDX example: +20 K changes all four). It also anchors the cold/hot-day sensitivity table. Accepted range 200-350 K. \emph{If blank:} T0 = T\_ref (no shift).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Case Wall Thickness, $t_{case}$} & \texttt{case\_\allowbreak{}thickness} & mm & 2 -- 100 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Wall thickness of motor case. Must be sufficient to withstand internal pressure with adequate safety factor. Calculated from hoop stress formula or specified directly. \emph{If blank:} Left blank, the solver sizes the wall itself from the Barlow thin-wall relation and declares that it did so.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Closure Bolt Count} & \texttt{closure\_\allowbreak{}bolt\_\allowbreak{}count} &  & 1 -- 200 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Number of bolts holding each closure against chamber pressure. Drives the separation and proof safety factors of the closure joint. \emph{If blank:} Leave empty if unknown - the joint is then reported as "not sized" instead of guessed.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Closure Bolt Size} & \texttt{closure\_\allowbreak{}bolt\_\allowbreak{}size} &  &  & M8 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Metric coarse thread size of the closure bolts (ISO 898-1 stress areas). Only used when a bolt count is given. Options: M4; M5; M6; M8; M10; M12; M14; M16; M20; M24.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Closure Bolt Class} & \texttt{closure\_\allowbreak{}bolt\_\allowbreak{}class} &  &  & 8.8 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Bolt property class: 8.8 / 10.9 / 12.9 (ISO 898-1) or A2-70 stainless (ISO 3506-1). Sets proof strength and therefore the preload. Options: 8.8; 10.9; 12.9; A2-70.} \\ \midrule
\end{longtable}}

\textbf{Throat Diameter Dt ((auto-filled after calculate)), $D_t$} & \texttt{throat\_\allowbreak{}diameter} & mm & 1 -- 500 & 15 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Nozzle throat diameter - critical parameter that determines chamber pressure and mass flow rate. Smaller throat = higher pressure. Must be sized for desired pressure and thrust.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Exit Diameter De ((auto-filled after calculate)), $D_e$} & \texttt{exit\_\allowbreak{}diameter} & mm & 1.5 -- 2500 & 35 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Nozzle exit diameter. Larger exit provides better expansion and higher specific impulse at altitude but increases nozzle weight and length.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Expansion Ratio \ensuremath{\varepsilon} (auto-filled after calculate), $\varepsilon$} & \texttt{expansion\_\allowbreak{}ratio} &  & 1 -- 25 & 5.44 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Ratio of exit area to throat area (Ae/At). Automatically calculated from diameters. Higher ratios provide better performance at altitude but risk flow separation at sea level.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Convergent Angle, $\alpha_c$} & \texttt{convergent\_\allowbreak{}angle} & \ensuremath{^\circ} & 10 -- 80 & 45 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Half-angle of convergent section approaching the throat. Affects flow uniformity and pressure losses in subsonic region.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Divergent Angle, $\alpha_d$} & \texttt{divergent\_\allowbreak{}angle} & \ensuremath{^\circ} & 5 -- 45 & 15 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Half-angle of divergent section after the throat. Larger angles cause flow separation, smaller angles increase nozzle length and weight.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Nozzle Efficiency \ensuremath{\eta}n, $\eta_n$} & \texttt{nozzle\_\allowbreak{}efficiency} &  & 0.8 -- 1 & 0.95 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Overall nozzle efficiency including divergence losses, friction, and heat transfer. Accounts for real-world performance reduction from ideal conditions.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Erosion Factor} & \texttt{erosion\_\allowbreak{}factor} & mm/s & 0 -- 5 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Throat erosion reference rate a\_ref in mm/s at the erosion law reference pressure (the empirical model scales it to the chamber pressure; the reference pressure is named in the erosion result). A value above 0 is sent and the solver erodes the throat with it during the burn; 0 means no erosion (rigid throat by choice). There is no single typical value - see the nozzle material properties line. Accepted range 0-5 mm/s. \emph{If blank:} (default): the solver keeps a rigid throat and, for a nozzle material with a published band (graphite), estimates the erosion and prints the rate it found at the chamber pressure in the warnings; for a material without a published band no erosion number is published.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Nozzle Material} & \texttt{nozzle\_\allowbreak{}material} &  &  & Graphite (isostatic, nozzle insert grade) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Material of the nozzle throat insert. The throat thermal check compares the adiabatic wall temperature at the throat (uncooled throat, worst case T\_wall \ensuremath{\rightarrow} T\_aw) with the allowable temperature of this material record; above it the verdict is EXCEEDS\_ALLOWABLE (critical warning). Throat erosion uses a published coefficient band only where one exists (shown below); otherwise a rigid throat is assumed and stated. Options come from the server material records; a name the server cannot resolve is rejected (no verdict is derived from another material). Phenolic is not offered: there is no sourced throat record and no ablation model. Options: Copper (OFHC, annealed); CuCrZr (C18150, aged); Graphite (isostatic, nozzle insert grade); Molybdenum TZM (stress-relieved); Tungsten (wrought, stress-relieved); Carbon-carbon (2D/3D C-C).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Chamber Pressure, $P_c$} & \texttt{chamber\_\allowbreak{}pressure} & bar &  & 40 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Operating pressure in the combustion chamber. Higher pressure increases performance but requires stronger casing. Safety factor of 2-4x is required for casing design.} \\ \midrule
\end{longtable}}

\textbf{Burn Rate Preset} & \texttt{burn\_\allowbreak{}rate\_\allowbreak{}preset} &  &  & KNDX -- KNO3/Dextrose 65/35 (Nakka fit) \\*

KNDX/KNSB: the piecewise regime table (Nakka 1999/2001 fits) is read at the instantaneous chamber pressure, and a, n show the regime at the current design pressure. Custom: the single a-n pair in the boxes below is used (for a propellant without a regime table this is its catalogue pair). The preset follows the "Propellant (catalogue record)" selector; choosing another propellant's preset switches the selector to it, so a regime table can never belong to a different propellant (the solver rejects such a mix). Editing a or n manually switches to Custom. Options: Custom (manual a, n); KNDX -- KNO3/Dextrose 65/35 (Nakka fit); KNSB -- KNO3/Sorbitol 65/35 (Nakka fit).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Burn Rate Coefficient (a), $a$} & \texttt{burn\_\allowbreak{}rate\_\allowbreak{}a} & m/\allowbreak{}s/\allowbreak{}bar\textasciicircum{}n &  & 0.0007876 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Burn-rate coefficient a of r [m/s] = a \ensuremath{\times} (P [bar])\textasciicircum{}n. With the Burn Rate Preset on a propellant's regime table (KNDX, KNSB) the solver reads the table at the instantaneous pressure and this box only shows the coefficient of the current regime; with Custom it is the a used in every step. Picking a catalogue record fills it (see the catalogue row for each propellant's value); typing here switches the preset to Custom. \emph{If blank:} The selected record's a is used.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Burn Rate Exponent (n), $n$} & \texttt{burn\_\allowbreak{}rate\_\allowbreak{}n} &  & -0.5 -- 1 & 0.688 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Pressure sensitivity exponent in burn rate law r=a\ensuremath{\times}P\textasciicircum{}n. Low n (0.2-0.4) gives stable combustion. High n (0.6+) can cause pressure instability. KN-sugar plateau/mesa regimes can have NEGATIVE n (burn rate drops with pressure) -- this is physical, from published fits.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Combustion Efficiency \ensuremath{\eta}c, $\eta_{c^*}$} & \texttt{combustion\_\allowbreak{}efficiency} &  & 0.5 -- 1 & 0.95 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} c* efficiency factor. Accounts for incomplete combustion and heat losses. Higher values indicate better propellant mixing and combustion completeness.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Nozzle Discharge Efficiency (Cf), $\eta_{C_F}$} & \texttt{cf\_\allowbreak{}efficiency} &  & 0.8 -- 1 & 0.98 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Cf efficiency factor accounting for nozzle losses including friction, heat transfer, and flow non-uniformities.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Overall Thrust Efficiency \ensuremath{\eta}overall} & \texttt{overall\_\allowbreak{}efficiency} &  & 0.5 -- 1 & 0.92 \\*

\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Flow discharge coefficient for mass flow through nozzle throat. Accounts for viscous effects and flow non-uniformities.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Kinetic Efficiency, $\eta_{kin}$} & \texttt{kinetic\_\allowbreak{}efficiency} &  & 0.8 -- 1 & 0.97 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Efficiency of converting thermal energy to kinetic energy in the nozzle. Accounts for incomplete expansion and non-ideal gas effects.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Divergence Loss Factor} & \texttt{divergence\_\allowbreak{}loss} &  & 0 -- 0.2 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Thrust loss due to non-axial flow in divergent nozzle section. Depends on divergent half-angle.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Two-Phase Loss Factor} & \texttt{two\_\allowbreak{}phase\_\allowbreak{}loss} &  & 0.8 -- 1 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Performance reduction due to solid particles (alumina) in exhaust gas. Particles have lower expansion efficiency than gas. \emph{If blank:} Left blank, the solver applies no user two-phase factor and declares that in isp\_loss\_breakdown.} \\ \midrule
\end{longtable}}

\subsection{Verdicts and warnings}

On the solid page every non-critical line is printed with the \ui{CHECK} tag
(Table~\ref{tab:siddet}). Example lines and their reading are in
Table~\ref{tab:u2-kontrol}. Gate rejections: a grain that does not fit the
case, a core larger than the grain, or a port area not larger than the throat
area is rejected by name; where applicable the smallest case that fits is
stated.

\subsection{Limits}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em]
  \item Below about 75~mm the delivered Isp can be optimistic; two-phase flow,
  heat loss and short-L* scale effects are not modelled.
  \item The two-phase correction is not verified and its status is declared.
  \item Throat erosion is estimated, not applied to the thrust curve.
  \item Star and finocyl grains are not exported to CAD; the export is refused
  with its reason.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Related sections}

Example~2 (Section~\ref{sec:uyg-kati}); Grain Section FEA
(Section~\ref{sec:guverte}); canonical bands (Appendix~\ref{sec:eke}).

\section{Liquid Engine Page}\label{sec:sivi}

\subsection{Purpose}

Sizes the thermochemistry, chamber, nozzle, injector, feed cycle
(\ui{Pressure-Fed}, \ui{Gas Generator}, \ui{Staged Combustion}, \ui{Full-Flow
Staged Combustion}, \ui{Expander Cycle}, \ui{Tap-Off Cycle}), regenerative or
film cooling and the wall of a bipropellant liquid engine; gives the throttle
map and the feed-line pressure budget.

\subsection{Screen}

\ekran{img/v3_0_5/sivi_form_cevrim_en.png}{Liquid page: \ui{3. FEED SYSTEM /
ENGINE CYCLE}. Note that the feed-pressure field is hidden in a turbopump
cycle.}{fig:sivi-form}

\subsection{Inputs}

In a regenerative chamber the wall has two layers: a channelled liner
(\ui{Chamber Material} and wall thickness) and a structural closeout shell
(closeout material and thickness; HRMA sizes it if empty). The wall
temperature field is a design target; the limit verdict uses the temperature
the solver reaches.

OXIDIZER)}.}{fig:sivi-yakit}

PARAMETERS}.}{fig:sivi-enj}

chamber material and wall (the liner in a regenerative chamber).}{fig:sivi-oda}

\textbf{Oxidizer Density \ensuremath{\rho}ox, $\rho_{ox}$} & \texttt{oxidizer\_\allowbreak{}density} & kg/m\textsuperscript{3} & 20 -- 2500 & 1141.16 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Oxidizer density at operating temperature. LOX: 1141, N2O4: 1443. Higher density oxidizers reduce tank volume and vehicle size, critical for spacecraft design. \emph{If blank:} Left blank, the value is auto-filled from the propellant table when the state solution resolves; if it does not resolve, the field stays empty.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Fuel Boiling Point} & \texttt{fuel\_\allowbreak{}boiling\_\allowbreak{}point} & K & 20 -- 900 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Fuel boiling point at 1 atm (K). Used only for the coolant-boiling check: if the regenerative coolant exit temperature exceeds it, a warning says the single-phase cooling model no longer applies. The propellant card above shows the property record's value for the selected fuel. A value left over from another fuel is cleared when the fuel changes. Accepted 20-900 K. \emph{If blank:} Leave it EMPTY and the check is not run; the results say so.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Fuel Viscosity} & \texttt{fuel\_\allowbreak{}viscosity} & Pa\ensuremath{\cdot}s & 1e-07 -- 10 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Fuel dynamic viscosity at operating temperature. Affects injection pressure drop and atomization. RP-1: 0.0012, LH2: 0.000013, Methane: 0.00011, MMH: 0.00085. Lower viscosity improves injection. Accepted range: 1e-7 to 10 Pa\ensuremath{\cdot}s (server band; outside it the request is rejected with a named 422). \emph{If blank:} Left blank, the value is auto-filled from the propellant table when the state solution resolves; if it does not resolve, the field stays empty.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Oxidizer Viscosity, $\mu_{ox}$} & \texttt{oxidizer\_\allowbreak{}viscosity} & Pa\ensuremath{\cdot}s & 1e-07 -- 10 & 0.0001947 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Oxidizer dynamic viscosity at operating temperature. LOX: 0.00019, N2O4: 0.00042. Higher viscosity increases injection pressure requirements and affects atomization quality. Accepted range: 1e-7 to 10 Pa\ensuremath{\cdot}s (server band; outside it the request is rejected with a named 422). \emph{If blank:} Left blank, the value is auto-filled from the propellant table when the state solution resolves; if it does not resolve, the field stays empty.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Fuel Heat Capacity Cp} & \texttt{fuel\_\allowbreak{}heat\_\allowbreak{}capacity} & J/\allowbreak{}kg\ensuremath{\cdot}K & 500 -- 20000 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Liquid fuel specific heat (J/kg\ensuremath{\cdot}K). Used by the regenerative-jacket bulk coolant temperature rise. A value left over from another fuel is cleared when the fuel changes. Accepted 500-20000 J/kg\ensuremath{\cdot}K. \emph{If blank:} Leave it EMPTY and HRMA uses its propellant table value for the selected fuel (RP-1 2090, LH2 14300, methane 3480 J/kg\ensuremath{\cdot}K; other fuels a declared 2000 J/kg\ensuremath{\cdot}K fallback) and states the source in the results.} \\ \midrule
\end{longtable}}

\textbf{Engine Cycle Type} & \texttt{engine\_\allowbreak{}cycle} &  &  & Pressure-Fed \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Turbopump drive method. Pressure-fed: simple, limited performance. Expander: LH2 only, high efficiency. Options: Pressure-Fed; Gas Generator; Staged Combustion; Full-Flow Staged Combustion; Expander Cycle; Tap-Off Cycle.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Preburner Type} & \texttt{preburner\_\allowbreak{}type} &  &  & Fuel-Rich \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Staged combustion runs its preburner either fuel-rich (RS-25, RD-0120) or oxidizer-rich (RD-180, NK-33). This sets the turbine drive gas and the pump pressure ladder. Full-flow staged combustion uses both and needs no choice here. Options: Fuel-Rich; Oxidizer-Rich.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Target Thrust, $F$} & \texttt{thrust} & N & 100 -- 10000000 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Target thrust level for the liquid engine. Small thrusters: 100-1000N, Medium engines: 1-100kN, Large boosters: 100kN-2MN (F-1). Accepted range: 100 N - 10 MN. Determines engine size, mass flow, and cooling requirements. \emph{If blank:} This field is a required design point: left blank, the request is refused by name.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Chamber Pressure Pc, $P_c$} & \texttt{chamber\_\allowbreak{}pressure} & bar & 10 -- 500 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Combustion chamber operating pressure. Higher pressure improves Isp but increases complexity. Pressure-fed: 10-50 bar, Gas Generator: 50-150 bar, Staged Combustion: 150-300 bar. Accepted range: 10-500 bar. \emph{If blank:} This field is a required design point: left blank, the request is refused by name.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Feed System Pressure, $P_{feed}$} & \texttt{feed\_\allowbreak{}pressure} & bar & 1 -- 1000 & 130 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Pressure-fed cycle: the tank pressure (bar). HRMA sizes the tanks and the feed-line and valve budget from it and checks it against the pressure the chamber needs (Pc + injector drop + cooling-jacket and line losses); a lower value is refused by name and the required minimum is stated. Not used in pump-fed (turbopump) cycles: the field is hidden there and not sent. Accepted 1-1000 bar. \emph{If blank:} Left blank in a pressure-fed cycle, the request is refused by name (no tank pressure is assumed).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Turbopump Efficiency \ensuremath{\eta}tp, $\eta_{tp}$} & \texttt{turbopump\_\allowbreak{}efficiency} & \% & 20 -- 95 & 75 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Combined efficiency of turbine and pump. Modern turbopumps: 65-85\%. Higher efficiency reduces power requirements and improves overall engine performance.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Generator Gas Temperature, $T_{GG}$} & \texttt{generator\_\allowbreak{}gas\_\allowbreak{}temp} & K & 400 -- 2500 & 1000 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Gas generator or preburner operating temperature for turbine drive. Affects turbine material requirements and efficiency.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Turbine Inlet Pressure, $P_{t,in}$} & \texttt{turbine\_\allowbreak{}inlet\_\allowbreak{}pressure} & bar & 1 -- 1000 & 150 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Turbine inlet pressure (bar), turbopump cycles only. When the turbine expansion ratio is also entered, the solver uses that ratio and only compares this value with the inlet pressure its cycle balance needs (a warning names both). Accepted 1-1000 bar. \emph{If blank:} Leave the expansion ratio empty and the ratio is solved from this pressure.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Turbine Expansion Ratio, $\pi_t$} & \texttt{turbine\_\allowbreak{}expansion\_\allowbreak{}ratio} &  & 1.2 -- 60 & 4 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Pressure ratio across turbine (inlet/exit). Higher ratios extract more energy but require more complex turbine design.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Feed Line Wall Thickness} & \texttt{feed\_\allowbreak{}line\_\allowbreak{}wall\_\allowbreak{}thickness} & mm & 0.1 -- 50 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Feed-line pipe wall thickness. HRMA sizes the line diameter for flow velocity but computes no wall thickness anywhere, so this is a user input. Needed for the elastic-pipe wave speed and the pipe pressure-rating check. \emph{If blank:} Leave empty if unknown - the water-hammer transient is then reported as NOT MODELLED instead of guessed.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Valve Closure Time} & \texttt{valve\_\allowbreak{}closure\_\allowbreak{}time\_\allowbreak{}ms} & ms & 0.1 -- 600000 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Main valve closure time for the water-hammer transient. Closure slower than the pipe period reduces the surge (Michaud). \emph{If blank:} Leave empty - the analysis then assumes instantaneous closure (full Joukowsky surge, the conservative upper bound) and declares that assumption.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Feed Line Length} & \texttt{feed\_\allowbreak{}line\_\allowbreak{}length\_\allowbreak{}m} & m & 0.05 -- 50 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Feed-line length from the tank outlet to the injector manifold. Together with the inner diameter it sets the feed-line inertance, which switches the chug (low-frequency) stability loop to its second-order form. \emph{If blank:} Leave empty if unknown - the chug analysis then runs without line inertia and declares that assumption instead of guessing a layout.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Feed Line Inner Diameter} & \texttt{feed\_\allowbreak{}line\_\allowbreak{}diameter\_\allowbreak{}mm} & mm & 0.5 -- 500 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Inner diameter of the feed line. The flow area for the feed-line inertance is derived from it as a circular duct. Accepted 0.5-500 mm. \emph{If blank:} Leave empty if unknown - the chug analysis then runs without line inertia and declares that assumption.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Feed Line Material (optional)} & \texttt{feed\_\allowbreak{}line\_\allowbreak{}material} &  &  & Default -- SS 304 assumed \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Pipe material of the feed lines: sets the elastic modulus for the water-hammer wave speed and the strength for the pipe pressure-rating check. Leave on default - stainless 304 is then assumed and the assumption is declared in the output. Options: Default -- SS 304 assumed; Stainless Steel 304; Stainless Steel 316; Aluminum 6061; Titanium Ti-6Al-4V; Inconel 718.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Tank Pressurization Gas (optional)} & \texttt{pressurization\_\allowbreak{}type} &  &  & Auto (default) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Tank pressurization gas choice. Sets the relieving-gas identity of the tank relief-valve sizing (helium unless nitrogen is chosen). Autogenous pressurization is sized numerically only for methane/LOX and LH2/LOX turbopump configurations; elsewhere the choice is echoed with its declared limits. Leave on auto for the standard stored-helium assumption. Options: Auto (default); Helium; Nitrogen; Autogenous (propellant vapor).} \\ \midrule
\end{longtable}}

\toprule
\textbf{Input} & \textbf{Identifier} & \textbf{Unit} & \textbf{Form limit} & \textbf{Form default} \\ \midrule

\textbf{Injector Type} & \texttt{injector\_\allowbreak{}type} &  &  & Unlike doublet (F-O impinging) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Injector element family; it selects the injector circuit model and so the hole plan, the impingement or spray geometry and the atomisation correlation. Unlike doublet (F-O impinging): each fuel jet hits an oxidizer jet (fuel and oxidizer holes in pairs, momentum ratio checked). Like-on-like doublet (F-F / O-O): fuel jets hit fuel jets and oxidizer jets hit oxidizer jets; each circuit has an even hole count and the two fans mix afterwards (no momentum-ratio criterion). Coaxial swirl: oxidizer pressure-swirl element with a concentric fuel stream. Showerhead: parallel axial jets, no impingement. Pintle: one central element, fuel through radial tip holes and oxidizer through the annulus around the post. The field always carries a choice; an API request without it is solved as the unlike doublet and says so. Options: Unlike doublet (F-O impinging); Like-on-like doublet (F-F / O-O); Coaxial Swirl; Showerhead; Pintle; Unlike doublet (F-O impinging).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Number of Injector Elements, $N_{el}$} & \texttt{injector\_\allowbreak{}elements} &  & 1 -- 20000 & 100 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Number of injection elements (count). It fixes the hole count of the injector circuits; the hole diameters then follow from the flow areas. Unlike doublet, showerhead, coaxial: holes per circuit (one fuel + one oxidizer hole per element). Like-on-like doublet: same-fluid PAIRS per circuit (two holes each), 1-60 because the circuit planner allows at most 120 holes per circuit; more is rejected, not clamped. Not used for the pintle (a single element; the field is hidden). Accepted band 1-20000. \emph{If blank:} Empty: each circuit plans the fewest holes inside its 0.5-2.5 mm diameter band and the answer says so.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Fuel Injection Velocity, $v_f$} & \texttt{fuel\_\allowbreak{}injection\_\allowbreak{}velocity} & m/s & 0.5 -- 300 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Fuel injection velocity (m/s). A value you enter changes no calculation: it is only compared with the solver value (deviation above 20 \% is flagged). Accepted 0.5-300 m/s. \emph{If blank:} HRMA computes it from the injector pressure drop, Cd and flow (orifice equation) and publishes it, so the field opens empty.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Oxidizer Injection Velocity, $v_{ox}$} & \texttt{oxidizer\_\allowbreak{}injection\_\allowbreak{}velocity} & m/s & 0.5 -- 300 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Oxidizer injection velocity (m/s). A value you enter changes no calculation: it is only compared with the solver value (deviation above 20 \% is flagged). Accepted 0.5-300 m/s. \emph{If blank:} HRMA computes it from the injector pressure drop, Cd and flow (orifice equation) and publishes it, so the field opens empty.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Fuel Orifice Diameter} & \texttt{fuel\_\allowbreak{}orifice\_\allowbreak{}diameter} & mm & 0.05 -- 50 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Fuel orifice diameter (mm). A value you enter changes no calculation: it is only compared with the solver value (deviation above 20 \% is flagged). Accepted 0.05-50 mm. \emph{If blank:} HRMA sizes the orifices from flow, pressure drop, Cd and element count and publishes them, so the field opens empty.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Oxidizer Orifice Diameter} & \texttt{oxidizer\_\allowbreak{}orifice\_\allowbreak{}diameter} & mm & 0.05 -- 50 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Oxidizer orifice diameter (mm). A value you enter changes no calculation: it is only compared with the solver value (deviation above 20 \% is flagged). Accepted 0.05-50 mm. \emph{If blank:} HRMA sizes the orifices from flow, pressure drop, Cd and element count and publishes them, so the field opens empty.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Injector Pressure Drop \ensuremath{\Delta}P, $\Delta P_{inj}$} & \texttt{injector\_\allowbreak{}pressure\_\allowbreak{}drop} & bar & 0.2 -- 200 & 20 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Absolute pressure drop across the injector, in bar. A number you type is used as bar and labelled "user input (injector pressure drop)". Accepted 0.2-200 bar: a value outside that band is refused by name and no design is published. A drop with dP/Pc outside 0.05-0.40 is calculated but warned (SP-8089 guideline). A larger drop improves mixing and stability but raises the required feed pressure. \emph{If blank:} Leave it EMPTY and HRMA sets the drop as chamber pressure x a dP/Pc factor of the injector type (impinging 0.22, coaxial 0.18, showerhead 0.28, pintle 0.15, other types 0.20); the result labels it "NASA SP-8089 dP/Pc ratio for the element type".} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Discharge Coefficient Cd, $C_d$} & \texttt{discharge\_\allowbreak{}coefficient} &  & 0.2 -- 1 & 0.7 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Accounts for real flow effects in orifices. Sharp-edged orifices: 0.6-0.65, Well-rounded: 0.8-0.85. Higher Cd reduces required pressure drop for given flow rate.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Injector Plate Material (optional)} & \texttt{injector\_\allowbreak{}material} &  &  & Not selected (plate check not run) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Material of the injector face plate. Used only in the injector plate structural check: a clamped circular plate (Roark Table 11.2, case 10b) of the chamber diameter under the injector pressure drop, with ASME PG-52 ligament efficiency from the fuel + oxidizer hole plan (all holes at the larger diameter, conservative). It gives the plate thickness that meets the Structural Safety Factor from the room-temperature yield strength; the page has no plate-thickness input. Not run for pintle, coaxial and swirl elements (no drilled-hole plan; the result says why). An unknown name is rejected. Options: Not selected (plate check not run); AISI 4130 low-alloy steel (normalized); Carbon steel (generic, A36-class); Stainless steel 304 (annealed); Stainless steel 316 (annealed); Aluminum 6061-T6; Titanium Ti-6Al-4V; Inconel 718 (aged); CuCrZr (C18150, aged); Aluminum 7075-T6; Aluminum 2024-T3; Stainless 17-4PH (H900); AISI 4340 low-alloy steel (normalized); Inconel 625 (annealed); Titanium CP Grade 2; Beryllium copper C17200 (aged, AT); Brass C36000 (free-cutting, H02); Magnesium AZ31B-H24. \emph{If blank:} Empty: the check is not run.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Pintle Post Diameter D\_p} & \texttt{pintle\_\allowbreak{}diameter} & mm & \ensuremath{\ge}\,0 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Outer diameter of the pintle post at its tip (D\_p, mm); the fuel tip holes are drilled into it and the oxidizer flows through the annulus around it. With the annulus area fixed by the oxidizer circuit, D\_p sets the annular gap t, and through the blockage factor the tip-hole count. Must be a finite positive length; the annulus bore D\_p + 2t must fit inside the chamber. \emph{If blank:} Empty: sized from the oxidizer flow with the annulus rule t = 0.05\ensuremath{\cdot}D\_p (HRMA choice, no literature value).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Oxidizer Annular Gap t} & \texttt{annular\_\allowbreak{}gap} & mm & \ensuremath{\ge}\,0 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Radial gap of the oxidizer annulus around the pintle post (t, mm). The annulus area pi\ensuremath{\cdot}(D\_p + t)\ensuremath{\cdot}t must equal the oxidizer circuit flow area: given alone, D\_p is solved from it; given with D\_p, the two must agree within 5\% (HRMA tolerance) or the design is rejected with the mismatch. \emph{If blank:} Empty: solved from the oxidizer flow area.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Fuel Tip Hole Count n (optional)} & \texttt{pintle\_\allowbreak{}radial\_\allowbreak{}hole\_\allowbreak{}count} &  & \ensuremath{\ge}\,1 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Number of radial fuel holes in the single row on the pintle tip (whole number \ensuremath{\ge} 1). The holes carry the fuel circuit flow area n\ensuremath{\cdot}pi\ensuremath{\cdot}d\textsuperscript{2}/4, so the hole diameter follows from n. \emph{If blank:} Empty: from the blockage factor n\ensuremath{\cdot}d/(pi\ensuremath{\cdot}D\_p) = 0.58 (HRMA choice, no literature value).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Fuel Tip Hole Diameter d} & \texttt{pintle\_\allowbreak{}radial\_\allowbreak{}hole\_\allowbreak{}diameter} & mm & \ensuremath{\ge}\,0 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Diameter of each radial fuel tip hole (d, mm). Given alone, the hole count is the nearest whole number for this diameter and the published diameter is the one that delivers the fuel circuit area exactly with that count; a plan more than 5\% off (also with a given count) is rejected with the nearest valid plans. \emph{If blank:} Empty: solved from the fuel flow area.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Skip Distance L\_s} & \texttt{skip\_\allowbreak{}distance} & mm & \ensuremath{\ge}\,0 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Axial distance from the annulus exit (injector face) to the axis of the tip-hole row (L\_s, mm; definition Dressler \& Bauer, AIAA 2000-3871). Geometry and CAD only: no performance model uses it. Must be shorter than the chamber. \emph{If blank:} Empty: L\_s = D\_p (HRMA choice, no literature value).} \\ \midrule
\end{longtable}}

\endlastfoot
\textbf{Chamber Diameter Dc ((optional)), $D_c$} & \texttt{chamber\_\allowbreak{}diameter} & mm & 10 -- 5000 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Internal diameter of combustion chamber. Larger chambers provide more residence time but increase weight.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Characteristic Length L*, $L^*$} & \texttt{characteristic\_\allowbreak{}length} & m & 0.3 -- 5 & 1.2 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} L* = Vc/At, where Vc is chamber volume and At is throat area. Indicates combustion residence time. Higher L* improves combustion efficiency.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Contraction Ratio \ensuremath{\varepsilon}c, $\varepsilon_c$} & \texttt{contraction\_\allowbreak{}ratio} &  & 1.5 -- 60 & 4 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Chamber area to throat area ratio (Ac/At). Higher ratios reduce chamber velocity and heat transfer but increase length. Higher for high chamber pressure engines.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Chamber Wall Thickness, $t_w$} & \texttt{chamber\_\allowbreak{}wall\_\allowbreak{}thickness} & mm & 0.2 -- 500 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Chamber wall thickness, mm. With Regenerative cooling this is the LINER: the hot-gas wall from the gas side to the channel base (the hot wall of the thermal chain and of the liner stress check); the coolant pressure is carried by the closeout (Closeout Thickness). With other cooling types it is the single structural wall that carries the chamber pressure. Server accepted range 0.2-500 mm. \emph{If blank:} Empty: Regenerative - HRMA uses a 1 mm liner and says so; other types - HRMA sizes the wall for the chamber pressure with your safety factor (next standard plate).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Chamber Material} & \texttt{chamber\_\allowbreak{}material} &  &  & Stainless steel 304 (annealed) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Chamber wall (liner) material. The options and the properties shown under the selector come from the HRMA materials record that the calculation reads: the chamber structural check (yield strength derated at the wall temperature) and the cooled-wall station march (conductivity, melting point) use this record. The same material is used along the cooled nozzle; a separate nozzle material analysis is not in this version. Options: Stainless steel 304 (annealed); Stainless steel 316 (annealed); Inconel 718 (aged); Inconel 625 (annealed); Aluminum 6061-T6; Copper (OFHC, annealed); CuCrZr (C18150, aged); AISI 4130 low-alloy steel (normalized).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Chamber Surface Roughness, $R_a$} & \texttt{chamber\_\allowbreak{}roughness} & \ensuremath{\mu}m Ra & 0.05 -- 100 & 3.2 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Internal surface roughness affects heat transfer and flow. Smooth surfaces (Ra \textless{} 1.6) reduce heat transfer but improve flow. Rougher surfaces enhance cooling but increase losses.} \\ \midrule
\end{longtable}}
