\begin{longtable}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{4.7cm}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{3.5cm}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{1.6cm}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{2.2cm}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{3.3cm}@{}}
\caption{Liquid page: 6. Nozzle and Cooling System}\label{tab:sivi-6}\\
\toprule
\textbf{Input} & \textbf{Identifier} & \textbf{Unit} & \textbf{Form limit} & \textbf{Form default} \\ \midrule
\endfirsthead
\toprule
\textbf{Input} & \textbf{Identifier} & \textbf{Unit} & \textbf{Form limit} & \textbf{Form default} \\ \midrule
\endhead
\multicolumn{5}{r@{}}{\footnotesize\itshape continued on next page}\\
\endfoot
\bottomrule
\endlastfoot
\textbf{Cooling Type} & \texttt{cooling\_\allowbreak{}type} &  &  & Regenerative (Fuel Cooling) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Method for managing high chamber temperatures (3000K+). Regenerative: fuel/coolant channels, best performance, complex. Ablative: sacrificial liner, simpler, limited reuse. Film: propellant film cooling. Radiation: space engines only. Options: Regenerative (Fuel Cooling); Ablative Liner; Film Cooling; Radiation Cooling; Dump Cooling.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Nozzle Expansion Ratio \ensuremath{\varepsilon}e, $\varepsilon$} & \texttt{nozzle\_\allowbreak{}expansion\_\allowbreak{}ratio} &  & 1.5 -- 300 & 50 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Exit area to throat area ratio (Ae/At). Higher ratios increase vacuum Isp but reduce sea-level performance. Limited by nozzle length and over-expansion.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Nozzle Type} & \texttt{nozzle\_\allowbreak{}type} &  &  & Conical (15\ensuremath{^\circ} half-angle) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Nozzle geometry type. Conical: simple, 15\ensuremath{^\circ} half-angle. Bell: optimized contour, shorter. Aerospike: altitude compensation, complex. Dual-bell: two expansion ratios. Extendable: deployable for space. Options: Conical (15\ensuremath{^\circ} half-angle); Bell Nozzle (80\% length); Bell Nozzle (60\% length); Aerospike; Dual-Bell.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Nozzle Throat Diameter, $D_t$} & \texttt{throat\_\allowbreak{}diameter} & mm & 1 -- 3000 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Nozzle throat diameter (mm). A value you enter changes no calculation: it is only compared with the solved throat (the result shows the solver value next to your entry and flags a deviation above 20 \%). Accepted 1-3000 mm. \emph{If blank:} HRMA sizes the throat itself from thrust, chamber pressure and c* (mass balance) and publishes it in the results, so the field opens empty.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Cooling Channel Count (optional)} & \texttt{cooling\_\allowbreak{}channels} &  & 4 -- 2000 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Number of regenerative cooling channels around chamber circumference. More channels provide better heat transfer but increase manufacturing complexity.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Closeout Material (optional)} & \texttt{closeout\_\allowbreak{}material} &  &  & HRMA default (Inconel 718) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Material of the closeout: the outer shell that covers the cooling channels of a regenerative wall and carries the coolant pressure (NASA SP-8087: electroformed or brazed closure). Shown with Regenerative cooling only. Options: HRMA default (Inconel 718); Inconel 718; Inconel 625; Stainless Steel 304; Stainless Steel 316. \emph{If blank:} Changes the closeout hoop check (yield at the closeout temperature, the highest coolant temperature) and, when Closeout Thickness is empty, the sized closeout thickness and the chamber mass; it does not change the thermal chain (the liner, Chamber Material, is the hot-gas wall). Empty: HRMA default Inconel 718, stated in the result.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Closeout Thickness} & \texttt{closeout\_\allowbreak{}thickness} & mm & 0.2 -- 500 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Closeout shell thickness, mm. Changes the closeout hoop stress (coolant pressure x outer radius / thickness) and its safety factor, the drawn wall stack (liner + channel depth + closeout) and the chamber mass. Accepted range 0.2-500 mm. Shown with Regenerative cooling only. \emph{If blank:} Empty: HRMA sizes it - hoop under the jacket coolant pressure at the largest jacket radius, yield at the closeout temperature / safety factor, 2 mm manufacturing floor, next standard plate - and states 'sized by HRMA'.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Coolant Flow Rate (\% of fuel flow)} & \texttt{coolant\_\allowbreak{}flow\_\allowbreak{}percent} &  & 5 -- 100 & 100 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Percentage of total fuel flow used for regenerative cooling. 100\% means all fuel passes through cooling channels. Lower percentages use bypass flow.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Film Cooling (\% of fuel flow)} & \texttt{film\_\allowbreak{}cooling\_\allowbreak{}percent} &  & 0 -- 30 & 0 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Film coolant flow as a percentage of the TOTAL fuel flow (burning core fuel + film). The film is fuel bled before the injector and laid along the chamber wall; it does not burn. Accepted range 0-30 \%. Effect: at constant thrust the film flow is ADDED to the core flow, so the total mass flow rises and the delivered Isp drops (Isp\_core x core flow / (core + film); the film's thrust contribution is neglected, a conservative lower bound). The film also absorbs part of the chamber wall heat. 0 \% with the Film Cooling type would leave the wall without any coolant and is rejected by name (no design is computed). \emph{If blank:} Empty: with the Film Cooling type HRMA applies a declared 5 \% default; with other cooling types there is no film.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Coolant Inlet Temperature, $T_{cool,in}$} & \texttt{coolant\_\allowbreak{}inlet\_\allowbreak{}temp} & K & 20 -- 700 & 300 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Temperature of coolant entering cooling system. Cryogenic fuels: near boiling point. Storable fuels: ambient temperature. Affects cooling capacity.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Maximum Wall Temperature, $T_{w,max}$} & \texttt{max\_\allowbreak{}wall\_\allowbreak{}temp} & K & 300 -- 3000 & 800 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Maximum allowable hot-side wall temperature. Limited by material properties and coking (for hydrocarbon fuels). Steel: 800K, Inconel: 1200K, Copper: 700K. Critical for engine life.} \\ \midrule
\end{longtable}}

A value you enter changes no calculation: it is only compared with the computed T/W (deviation above 20 \% is flagged). Accepted 1-500. \emph{If blank:} HRMA computes the engine T/W from its own dry-mass estimate and publishes it, so the field opens empty.} \\ \midrule

Human-rated: 4.0, Unmanned: 2.5-3.0, Expendable: 1.4-2.0. Covers pressure, thermal, and dynamic loads.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Closure Bolt Count (optional)} & \texttt{closure\_\allowbreak{}bolt\_\allowbreak{}count} &  & 1 -- 200 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Number of bolts holding the injector/closure flange against chamber pressure. Drives the separation and proof safety factors of the closure joint. \emph{If blank:} Leave empty if unknown - the joint is then reported as "not sized" instead of guessed.} \\ \midrule

\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} How the engine is attached to the vehicle. Used only by the "Gimbal Mount Loads" panel in the results (a fixed mount gives a not-applicable verdict there); the engine calculation does not read it. Options: 2-Axis Gimbal Mount; 1-Axis Gimbal Mount; Fixed Mount; Flexible Joint.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Gimbal Range} & \texttt{gimbal\_\allowbreak{}range} & \ensuremath{\pm} degrees & 0 -- 45 & 8 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Maximum gimbal deflection angle (\ensuremath{\pm} degrees). Used only by the "Gimbal Mount Loads" panel in the results (side force = thrust x sin(angle)); the engine calculation does not read it. \emph{If blank:} Left blank, the panel states the missing input instead of assuming one.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Gimbal Actuator Arm} & \texttt{gimbal\_\allowbreak{}actuator\_\allowbreak{}arm} & m & \ensuremath{\ge}\,0 & (blank) \\*

Sets the actuator stroke and the force needed to react a given moment. \emph{If blank:} Leave blank if unknown - no default is assumed and the load chain is not computed.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Mount Ring Offset} & \texttt{gimbal\_\allowbreak{}ring\_\allowbreak{}offset} & m & \ensuremath{\ge}\,0 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Axial distance from the gimbal pivot to the mount ring plane. The side force acting over this arm bends the ring. \emph{If blank:} Leave blank for a ring in the pivot plane (h = 0), where the bending moment is zero by construction.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Mount Bolt Circle Diameter} & \texttt{gimbal\_\allowbreak{}bolt\_\allowbreak{}circle} & mm & \ensuremath{\ge}\,0 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Diameter of the bolt circle carrying the engine on the mount ring. Together with the bolt count it converts the ring moment into a per-bolt load. \emph{If blank:} Leave blank to skip the per-bolt loads.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Mount Bolt Count (optional)} & \texttt{gimbal\_\allowbreak{}bolt\_\allowbreak{}count} &  & \ensuremath{\ge}\,3 & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Number of equally spaced bolts on the bolt circle. The bolt-circle formula needs at least 3; fewer are rejected rather than extrapolated. \emph{If blank:} Leave blank to skip the per-bolt loads.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Expected Engine Life} & \texttt{engine\_\allowbreak{}life\_\allowbreak{}cycles} & cycles & 1 -- 100000 & 10 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Number of start/stop cycles before refurbishment. Reusable engines need higher life. Expendable: 1-2 cycles, Reusable booster: 10-100 cycles, Spacecraft: 50-1000 cycles.} \\ \midrule
\end{longtable}}

After an engine calculation (and again when the trajectory is computed), unless you typed in this field, it is filled from the flown vehicle: the engine flying inert mass (engine dry + propellant tank structure + reserve propellant, the same number the Launch Site flies) + the propellant mass. Add airframe and payload to both masses to fly a real vehicle; a value you type is kept. Must be smaller than the initial mass. \emph{If blank:} Empty: the trajectory asks for it by name (no mass is assumed).} \\ \midrule

Not filled from the engine calculation. \emph{If blank:} Empty or not a number: the field is not sent and the trajectory endpoint refuses the run, naming the field (no value is assumed).} \\ \midrule

\subsection{Verdicts and warnings}

\begin{table}[htbp]
\centering\small
\caption{Liquid-specific verdicts and declarations}\label{tab:sivi-hukum}
\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{4.6cm}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{6.0cm}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5.0cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{On screen} & \textbf{Meaning} & \textbf{Action} \\
\midrule
\ui{CARBON DEPOSIT} & RP-1 gas-side deposit resistance applied; hot-wall temperature with the deposit and where it spalls. & Compare the spalled-zone temperature with the melting limit. \\
\ui{COKING RISK} & Coolant-side wall above the 561~K warning level; 728~K (NASA SP-8087) is the critical limit. & Lower the coolant-side temperature. \\
\ui{PROPERTY RANGE (WALL)} & Outside the coolant property table band; the coolant-side coefficient is a conservative lower bound. & \\
\ui{INPUT} lines & Input consistency or a missing input (boiling point, turbine pressures). & Complete or correct the input. \\
Chug verdict \ui{MARGINAL} (pintle) & The two atomisation scales give different stability verdicts. & Raise the stability margin with the injector pressure drop or the chamber volume. \\
Throttle note (separation) & Below a given throttle the nozzle separates at sea level; the sea-level Isp of those points is not published. & \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\ekran{img/v3_0_5/sivi_pintle_chug_sinirda_en.png}{With the pintle selected,
the chug verdict is \ui{MARGINAL}: the two atomisation scales give different
verdicts.}{fig:sivi-sinirda}

Gate rejections: out-of-band inputs, a pressure-fed tank below the required
pressure and a turbopump cycle whose power balance does not close are rejected
by name. With film cooling there is no regenerative jacket and the film flow is
subtracted from the delivered Isp; 0\,\% film is rejected.

\subsection{Limits}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em]
  \item The delivered Isp is a preliminary-design estimate (92.9--93.9\,\% of
  the CEA ideal Isp over the CEA comparison grid).
  \item In the two-layer wall, low-cycle fatigue, creep, liner--shell thermal
  mismatch, bond strength and buckling are not modelled and are named in the
  response. CAD draws both layers, not the cooling channels.
  \item Turbopump maps, cavitation, rotordynamics, start-up and shut-down
  transients are not included.
  \item Channel sizing applies the 40~m/s coolant velocity target (NASA
  SP-8087) also to supercritical hydrogen; the result errs on the safe side
  (hotter predicted wall).
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Related sections}

Example~3 (Section~\ref{sec:uyg-sivi}); Regenerative Cooling panel
(Table~\ref{tab:p-sogutma}); canonical bands (Appendix~\ref{sec:eke}).

\section{NASA CEA Comparison}\label{sec:cea}

The three designer pages show a NASA CEA comparison block at the end of the
results. RocketCEA (NASA CEA, Gordon and McBride, NASA RP-1311) is run at the
design point of the run: same chamber pressure, O/F and expansion ratio.

\begin{table}[htbp]
\centering\small
\caption{Content of the CEA comparison by motor type}\label{tab:cea}
\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{2.2cm}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{13.4cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Motor} & \textbf{Content} \\
\midrule
Hybrid & HRMA's own equilibrium (Cantera) against CEA; delivered $c^*$ on a separate row. H\textsubscript{2}O\textsubscript{2} is taken as 100\,\% pure and the block says so. \\
Solid & For catalogue propellants of known composition, catalogue values and the ideal nozzle next to CEA at the motor's own pressure. For a propellant of uncertain composition the block gives the reason and no number. \\
Liquid & CEA ideal values next to HRMA's delivered values; the efficiency that explains each difference is stated (Table~\ref{tab:u3-cea}). \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\ekran{img/v3_0_5/hibrit_cea_karsilastirma_en.png}{\ui{NASA CEA Comparison} in
the hybrid: HRMA equilibrium, CEA and difference.}{fig:cea-hib}

\ekran{img/v3_0_5/kati_cea_karsilastirma_en.png}{\ui{NASA CEA Comparison} in
the solid: catalogue values and the ideal nozzle next to CEA at the motor's own
pressure.}{fig:cea-kati}

The comparison is a code verification, not a validation. It gives the same
input to two codes and shows that the two codes agree; it does not show how a
real motor will burn. Measured agreement over a grid run with CEA2 (RocketCEA
1.2.1) and NASA CEA v3 (3.3.4) (the two references differ by at most
0.001\,\%): in the hybrid 4532 of 4536 rows within 0.5\,\% ($T_c$ within
0.12\,\%, $c^*$ within 0.04\,\%), in liquid thermochemistry 1559 of 1559 rows,
in the solid 221 of 224 rows. $\Delta\% = 100\,(\text{HRMA} -
\text{CEA})/\text{CEA}$; no pass/fail threshold is applied and the comparison
changes no design number.

% =====================================================================
\section{Analysis Dock and Analysis Center}\label{sec:guverte}

\subsection{Purpose}

Runs detailed analyses on the motor of the main calculation. Panel inputs are
filled from the last calculation; every field can be changed and the request
is always built from the fields visible on screen.

\subsection{Screen}

\ekran{img/v3_0_5/hibrit_guverte_termal_en.png}{\ui{ANALYSIS DOCK}: category
tabs, the prefilled inputs of the selected panel and the value-source badges.
The \ui{ANALYSIS CENTER} is below this section.}{fig:guverte}

\subsection{Common contract}

The dock carries panels in eleven categories: \ui{THERMAL}, \ui{STRUCTURAL},
\ui{SAFETY}, \ui{PERFORMANCE}, \ui{PRESSURE VESSEL}, \ui{FLOW},
\ui{VALIDATION}, \ui{FEED SYSTEM}, \ui{COMPARE}, \ui{UNCERTAINTY},
\ui{CORRELATION}. The layout is chosen as \ui{Tabs} or \ui{Grid}. Each panel has
a \ui{Run Analysis} button, value-source badges, a listing of the fields the
panel sends and a \ui{What changed} block listing the differences between two
consecutive runs.

\begin{table}[htbp]
\centering\small
\caption{Value-source badges}\label{tab:rozet}
\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{3.4cm}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{12.2cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Badge} & \textbf{Meaning} \\
\midrule
\ui{COMPUTED} & The value was filled from the main calculation's solution for this design. \\
\ui{USER} & The user entered or changed the value; later prefills do not overwrite it. \\
\ui{ASSUMED} & The value was not solved here: a default, a literature value or a choice. \\
\ui{NOT MODELLED} & No value was computed for this quantity. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

If a required field is empty the request is not sent and the screen says
\ui{Required fields are empty: \ldots{} The request was not sent}. If the
material used by the solver is not in the panel's material list the request is
not sent either: a safety verdict is not issued on a material other than the
one the motor was computed with.

A panel result is read in this order:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=1.6em]
  \item The status line: was a verdict issued or withheld; if withheld, the reason.
  \item The input badges: \ui{ASSUMED} inputs show that part of the result
  comes from an assumption.
  \item The numbers and their bands. Numbers without a threshold are printed
  without colour; they are measurements, not verdicts.
  \item The list of items not modelled: the physics outside the panel's scope.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{Dock panels}

\begin{longtable}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{3.2cm}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{3.6cm}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{4.2cm}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{4.6cm}@{}}
\caption{Analysis Dock panels}\label{tab:paneller}\\
\toprule
\textbf{Category} & \textbf{Panel} & \textbf{Outputs} & \textbf{Verdict and limits} \\
\midrule\endfirsthead
\toprule
\textbf{Category} & \textbf{Panel} & \textbf{Outputs} & \textbf{Verdict and limits} \\
\midrule\endhead
\bottomrule\endlastfoot
\ui{THERMAL} & Thermal Safety (Bartz heat transfer and wall temperatures) & Gas-side heat-transfer coefficient, throat and chamber heat flux, wall temperatures, material-limit chart. & The wall temperature is compared with the material's allowable temperature. The $\gamma$ input is accepted in the band 1.05--1.67; outside it is rejected, not clipped. If empty, the repository default 1.20 is used and the result states \kod{gamma\_\allowbreak{}source: repo\_\allowbreak{}default}. An ambient temperature outside 180--340~K is rejected. \\
\ui{THERMAL} & Thermal Protection (ablative, heat sink, radiation cooled) & Three modes: ablative liner (Q*), heat-sink wall (1D), radiation-cooled extension. In ablative mode: recession rate, total recession, required liner thickness, Q* used, mean heat flux and total heat load. & A steady Q* model (\ui{SIMPLIFIED MODEL}). No thickness is published, and the reason is given, in two cases: with no net heating (recovery temperature below the ablation temperature; solid example) and when the recession rate exceeds the model's validity ceiling of 0.35~mm/s (\ui{MODEL NOT VALID}; 1.200~mm/s in the hybrid example, 1.017~mm/s in the liquid example). Zero recession is not zero thickness. \\
\ui{THERMAL} & Regenerative Cooling (1D station march, Bartz and Dittus--Boelter), liquid only & Gas- and coolant-side temperatures, heat flux and pressure drop station by station. & The coolant-side film coefficient is taken from a literature band. With dump cooling no jacket numbers are published. \\
\ui{STRUCTURAL} & Structural Safety (pressure vessel, buckling, fatigue) & Stress components and safety factors, buckling, fatigue, thermal stress. & If HRMA sized the wall the verdict is withheld. A wall entered by the user that misses the target receives a verdict (\ui{UNSAFE}); one that meets it does not make the response as a whole accepted, because the closure and nozzle stations are not verified in this panel (Section~\ref{sec:uyg-kati}). Without a declared external-pressure load case buckling is \ui{NOT\_EVALUATED}. Burn time is not used by this model, and this is declared. \\
\ui{STRUCTURAL} & Bolted Joint (Shigley) & Recommended tightening torque, preload and its $\pm$25\,\% scatter, proof safety factor, overload factor $n_L$, separation factor $n_0$, load sharing. & Proof and yield safety are evaluated at the upper end of the preload scatter and separation at the lower end (assumptions on screen: Shigley Ch.~8, NASA-STD-5020A). Member crushing under the bolt head is checked; it is flagged in the hybrid example (aluminium member). Bolt count, size and grade are the panel defaults (\ui{ASSUMED} badge, 8 × M8, 8.8): the result is an example joint until the motor's actual joint is entered. \\
\ui{SAFETY} & Comprehensive Safety (risk assessment and pressure vessel) & Two separate verdicts: \ui{MOTOR DESIGN RISK} and \ui{FACILITY / SITING HAZARD}. Risk score on six axes (1--5: structural, pressure, thermal, explosive, toxic, fire), 5×5 risk matrix, pressure vessel summary, TNT equivalent and facility distances. & An axis that cannot be evaluated is shown as \ui{NOT MODELLED} and left out of the score; the risk level is then partial and no acceptability verdict is given (a missing evaluation is not a low risk). Examples: hybrid and solid motor risk LOW, facility hazard \ui{NOT\_EVALUATED}; liquid motor risk LOW, facility hazard HIGH. For liquid pairs the TNT equivalent is taken from 14 CFR Part 420, Appendix E, Table E-5 (10\,\% of the propellant mass for a test stand in the liquid example, 29.745~kg); a liquid pair not in the table uses 0.35, declared as an HRMA choice. In the hybrid and KNDX solid examples the explosive class is \ui{Not modelled (no sourced TNT equivalent)}. Without the required dimensions no safety verdict is produced. Regulatory compliance is not assessed. \\
\ui{PERFORMANCE} & Advanced Performance (3D surface in hybrid and liquid; Mach contour and heat flux in solid) & Isp--$P_c$--O/F surface, Mach contour, heat flux. & No 3D performance surface in the solid: O/F is not a design variable. \\
\ui{PRESSURE VESSEL} & Pressure Vessel (sizing, MAWP, burst pressure) & Status, design code (AIAA S-080 or ASME VIII Div~1), required and used wall, MAWP, predicted burst pressure and margin, pressure ladder (MEOP, proof, hydrostatic test, required burst), head thicknesses (ASME UG-32), temperature derating. & With the wall empty, the thickness meeting both the code minimum and a 1.2 margin against the required burst pressure is sized and stated in a warning. The burst pressure is the smaller of the Faupel thick-wall and the thin-wall plastic-limit relations; it is a model estimate, not a test. The material is the case material on the solid page (\ui{COMPUTED}); on the hybrid and liquid pages it is the panel default (Aluminum 6061-T6, \ui{ASSUMED} badge): change the field to check the motor's material. \\
\ui{FLOW} & Nozzle Flow (quasi-1D compressible) & Regime, pressure and Mach along the axis; the \ui{IDEAL} cards ($c^*$ efficiency and discharge coefficient 1: $C_F$, thrust, mass flow, $c^*$); effective $C_F$ and 1D thrust; the thrust, mass flow, $c^*$ and $C_F$ the motor delivers in a separate block. & With any of the six required fields empty the request is rejected. The effective $C_F$ is compared with the $C_F$ of the main result; the thrust cross-check is stated as well (Section~\ref{sec:uyg-hibrit}). \\
\ui{VALIDATION} & User Data Validation (static-fire CSV) & Differences in total impulse, peak and average thrust, burn time; NRMSE. & Relative difference (prediction $-$ measurement)/measurement. The score is the larger of the impulse difference and NRMSE; if the server sends no band the card is not coloured. \\
\ui{FEED SYSTEM} & Feed System (slosh, pressurant, water hammer) & Slosh frequency, pressurant mass, water-hammer peak pressure. & The fields are filled only from the motor's own result (they stay empty for a solid motor); the value used for an optional field left empty is declared under \kod{defaults\_\allowbreak{}applied}, and an empty required field rejects the request by name. The water-hammer map covers LOX, LH2, methane, MMH, UDMH, N\textsubscript{2}O\textsubscript{4} and N\textsubscript{2}O; no block is produced for H\textsubscript{2}O\textsubscript{2}. \\
\ui{COMPARE} & Comparative Analysis & Saved configurations side by side, two designs overlaid. & Only relative changes above the threshold are marked. \\
\ui{UNCERTAINTY} & Uncertainty Quantification (Monte Carlo) & Analysis level and seed; run summary (sample count, failed samples, duration, sampler); sampled input distributions; for each output P50, the [P5, P95] band, the nominal value and $\sigma$; distribution plot and sensitivity tornado (Spearman rank correlation). & The band is only the spread produced by the sampled inputs: model-form uncertainty is not included and it is not a confidence interval for the real motor; the screen says so in the \ui{How to read the band} row. An output insensitive to the sampled inputs gets no distribution (hybrid example: thrust and total impulse, since thrust and burn time are inputs). Correlations inside the noise floor are not ranked as effects. \\
\ui{CORRELATION} & Experimental Correlation & Deviation of the model against the shipped static-fire database. & Checks the model, not the user's motor. \\
\end{longtable}

\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Supplied cold-side (outer) wall temperature, K (\textgreater{} 0, not above the hot side; send it together with the hot side). Sets the through-wall gradient of the thermal stress. Filled together with the hot side from the motor result (solid: the same case temperature, a lumped case has no gradient). \emph{If blank:} The bare-wall equilibrium gives the verdict.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Wall protection} & \texttt{ad\_\allowbreak{}f\_\allowbreak{}thermal\_\allowbreak{}wall\_\allowbreak{}protection} &  &  & None (bare wall) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Protection of the chamber wall. None: the bare-wall verdict. Ablative liner: when the bare wall fails, HRMA sizes one ablative liner for the chamber wall (Level-1 Q*, the same sizing as the hybrid motor's chamber liner) and the verdict becomes LINER REQUIRED (warning); if no liner can be sized, the bare-wall verdict stands. Filled from the motor result after a calculation: a hybrid whose chamber zones are all protected selects Ablative liner. Ignored when supplied wall temperatures are given. Options: None (bare wall); Ablative liner sized by HRMA (Level-1 Q*).} \\ \midrule
\end{longtable}}

\textbf{[R] Emissivity Override (blank = material)} & \texttt{ad\_\allowbreak{}f\_\allowbreak{}protection\_\allowbreak{}emissivity} &  &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} [R] Surface emissivity, 0--1. Overrides the material's emissivity in the radiation balance. Options: 1.00 -- full radiography; 0.85 -- spot radiography; 0.70 -- no radiography.} \\ \midrule

\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} End-cap (head) shape: 2:1 ellipsoidal, torispherical or hemispherical. Selects the head thickness formula (changes head thickness and margin). Not filled from the motor result. Options: 2:1 Ellipsoidal; Torispherical; Hemispherical.} \\ \midrule
\end{longtable}}

{\small
\begin{longtable}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{4.7cm}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{3.5cm}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{1.6cm}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{2.2cm}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{3.3cm}@{}}
\caption{Dock: Nozzle Flow panel inputs}\label{tab:p-akis}\\
\toprule
\textbf{Input} & \textbf{Identifier} & \textbf{Unit} & \textbf{Form limit} & \textbf{Form default} \\ \midrule
\endfirsthead
\toprule
\textbf{Input} & \textbf{Identifier} & \textbf{Unit} & \textbf{Form limit} & \textbf{Form default} \\ \midrule
\endhead
\multicolumn{5}{r@{}}{\footnotesize\itshape continued on next page}\\
\endfoot
\bottomrule
\endlastfoot
\textbf{Fidelity Level} & \texttt{ad\_\allowbreak{}f\_\allowbreak{}flow\_\allowbreak{}fidelity} &  &  & Engineering \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Flow solution fidelity: fast or engineering. Selects the quasi-1D nozzle solver level of /api/flow-analysis. Not filled from the motor result. Options: Fast Screening; Engineering.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Kinetic Model} & \texttt{ad\_\allowbreak{}f\_\allowbreak{}flow\_\allowbreak{}kinetic\_\allowbreak{}fidelity} &  &  & Engineering (JANNAF-style) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Kinetic model level: fast or engineering. Selects the kinetic-efficiency model. Not filled from the motor result. Hybrid motors only: not shown for solid and liquid motors (the kinetics chain has no chemistry for them). Options: Fast (equilibrium reference); Engineering (JANNAF-style); Cantera finite-rate kinetics.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Chamber Pressure} & \texttt{ad\_\allowbreak{}f\_\allowbreak{}flow\_\allowbreak{}chamber\_\allowbreak{}pressure} & bar &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Chamber pressure, bar. Stagnation pressure of the nozzle flow (changes flow and kinetic efficiency). Filled from the motor result after a calculation (when the result provides it), unless you edit it. \emph{If blank:} Not sent; the endpoint then refuses with 422 incomplete\_flow\_input naming the field (no server default is assumed).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Chamber Temperature} & \texttt{ad\_\allowbreak{}f\_\allowbreak{}flow\_\allowbreak{}chamber\_\allowbreak{}temperature} & K &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Chamber temperature, K. Stagnation temperature of the nozzle flow. Filled from the motor result after a calculation (when the result provides it), unless you edit it. \emph{If blank:} Not sent; the endpoint then refuses with 422 incomplete\_flow\_input naming the field (no server default is assumed).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Gamma (frozen)} & \texttt{ad\_\allowbreak{}f\_\allowbreak{}flow\_\allowbreak{}gamma} &  &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Frozen ratio of specific heats \ensuremath{\gamma}. Sets the area--Mach relation (changes flow and kinetic efficiency). Filled from the motor result after a calculation (when the result provides it), unless you edit it. \emph{If blank:} Not sent; the endpoint then refuses with 422 incomplete\_flow\_input naming the field (no server default is assumed).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Molecular Weight} & \texttt{ad\_\allowbreak{}f\_\allowbreak{}flow\_\allowbreak{}molecular\_\allowbreak{}weight} & g/mol &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Gas molecular weight, g/mol (\textgreater{} 0). Sets the gas constant of the flow. Filled from the motor result after a calculation (when the result provides it), unless you edit it. \emph{If blank:} Not sent; the endpoint then refuses with 422 incomplete\_flow\_input naming the field (no server default is assumed).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Throat Diameter} & \texttt{ad\_\allowbreak{}f\_\allowbreak{}flow\_\allowbreak{}throat\_\allowbreak{}diameter} & m &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Throat diameter, m (\textgreater{} 0). Sets the throat area and mass flow. Filled from the motor result after a calculation (when the result provides it), unless you edit it. \emph{If blank:} Not sent; the endpoint then refuses with 422 incomplete\_flow\_input naming the field (no server default is assumed).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Exit Diameter} & \texttt{ad\_\allowbreak{}f\_\allowbreak{}flow\_\allowbreak{}exit\_\allowbreak{}diameter} & m &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Nozzle exit diameter, m (must exceed the throat diameter). Sets the expansion ratio of the solution. Filled from the motor result (or throat \ensuremath{\times} \ensuremath{\surd}expansion ratio) after a calculation, unless you edit it. \emph{If blank:} Not sent; the endpoint then refuses with 422 incomplete\_flow\_input naming the field (no server default is assumed).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Ambient Pressure} & \texttt{ad\_\allowbreak{}f\_\allowbreak{}flow\_\allowbreak{}ambient\_\allowbreak{}pressure} & Pa &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Ambient (back) pressure, Pa (\ensuremath{\ge} 0 and below the chamber pressure). Sets the exit regime (over/under-expansion, separation) and thrust. Filled after a calculation with the design ambient pressure the motor's nozzle was solved against (nozzle\_design.performance.ambient\_pressure, bar \ensuremath{\rightarrow} Pa), unless you edit it. \emph{If blank:} Not sent; the endpoint then refuses with 422 incomplete\_flow\_input naming the field (no server default is assumed).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Axial Stations (30-60)} & \texttt{ad\_\allowbreak{}f\_\allowbreak{}flow\_\allowbreak{}n\_\allowbreak{}stations} &  &  & 45 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Number of axial grid stations, whole number (30--60). Resolution of the quasi-1D solution; values outside 30--60 are clamped to that range (nozzle\_flow\_1d.py N\_STATIONS\_MIN/MAX), a fractional count is rejected (400). Not filled from the motor result. \emph{If blank:} The request is not sent and the field is named.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{O/F Ratio (kinetics)} & \texttt{ad\_\allowbreak{}f\_\allowbreak{}flow\_\allowbreak{}of\_\allowbreak{}ratio} &  &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} O/F mass ratio for the kinetics model (hybrid motors only). Changes only the kinetic efficiency. Filled from the motor result after a calculation, unless you edit it. Not shown for solid and liquid motors. \emph{If blank:} The request is not sent and the field is named (no default ratio is assumed).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Fuel (kinetics)} & \texttt{ad\_\allowbreak{}f\_\allowbreak{}flow\_\allowbreak{}fuel\_\allowbreak{}type} &  &  & -- select -- \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Fuel for the kinetics model (hybrid motors only). Selects the fuel of the kinetic-efficiency chain; it does not change the quasi-1D flow solution. Filled from the motor result after a calculation (the motor's fuel\_type), unless you edit it. Only the hybrid fuels the kinetics chain knows are listed; a motor fuel outside the list stops the request and names it. Not shown for solid and liquid motors (the kinetics chain has no chemistry for them). Options: -- select --; HTPB; Paraffin; PE; PMMA; ABS; PLA. \emph{If blank:} The request is not sent and the field is named.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Oxidizer (kinetics)} & \texttt{ad\_\allowbreak{}f\_\allowbreak{}flow\_\allowbreak{}oxidizer\_\allowbreak{}type} &  &  & -- select -- \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Oxidizer for the kinetics model (hybrid motors only). Selects the oxidizer of the kinetic-efficiency chain; it does not change the quasi-1D flow solution. Filled from the motor result after a calculation (the oxidizer the motor's combustion chain used), unless you edit it. A motor oxidizer outside the list stops the request and names it. Not shown for solid and liquid motors. Options: -- select --; N2O; LOX; H2O2. \emph{If blank:} The request is not sent and the field is named.} \\ \midrule
\end{longtable}}

\caption{Dock: Feed System panel inputs (slosh, pressurant, water hammer)}\label{tab:p-besleme}\\
\toprule
\textbf{Input} & \textbf{Identifier} & \textbf{Unit} & \textbf{Form limit} & \textbf{Form default} \\ \midrule

\textbf{Input} & \textbf{Identifier} & \textbf{Unit} & \textbf{Form limit} & \textbf{Form default} \\ \midrule

\multicolumn{5}{r@{}}{\footnotesize\itshape continued on next page}\\
\endfoot
\bottomrule
\endlastfoot
\textbf{Tank Radius} & \texttt{feed\_\allowbreak{}slosh\_\allowbreak{}radius} & m &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Tank radius, m (\textgreater{} 0). /api/slosh-analysis uses it for the sloshing modes. After a calculation it is filled from the motor result unless you edit it (hybrid: half the tank diameter of the run's oxidizer\_tank\_slosh block; liquid: the radius of the run's oxidizer-tank slosh block, propellant\_tanks.oxidizer\_tank.slosh). \emph{If blank:} Not sent; the endpoint rejects the request naming this field (required).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Fill Height} & \texttt{feed\_\allowbreak{}slosh\_\allowbreak{}fill\_\allowbreak{}height} & m &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Liquid fill height, m (\textgreater{} 0). Enters the sloshing frequency and mass. After a calculation it is filled from the motor result unless you edit it (hybrid: the fill height of the run's oxidizer\_tank\_slosh block; liquid: the fill height of the run's oxidizer-tank slosh block). \emph{If blank:} Not sent; the endpoint rejects the request naming this field (required).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Axial Acceleration} & \texttt{feed\_\allowbreak{}slosh\_\allowbreak{}g\_\allowbreak{}eff} & m/s\textsuperscript{2} &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Axial acceleration, m/s\textsuperscript{2} (\textgreater{} 0). Restoring acceleration of the slosh modes. Filled from the run's own slosh block (hybrid and liquid: the constant standard 1 g declared there). \emph{If blank:} Not sent; the endpoint uses standard gravity g0 = 9.80665 m/s\textsuperscript{2} and lists it below the result as a defaulted field.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Propellant Density} & \texttt{feed\_\allowbreak{}slosh\_\allowbreak{}fluid\_\allowbreak{}density} & kg/m\textsuperscript{3} &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Propellant density, kg/m\textsuperscript{3} (\textgreater{} 0). Sets the sloshing mass and forces. After a calculation it is filled from the motor result unless you edit it (hybrid: the liquid density of the run's oxidizer\_tank\_slosh block; liquid: the oxidizer density of the run, the density its slosh block used). \emph{If blank:} Not sent; the endpoint computes the modes without a liquid mass.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Baffle Width w/R} & \texttt{feed\_\allowbreak{}slosh\_\allowbreak{}baffle\_\allowbreak{}width\_\allowbreak{}ratio} &  &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Ring baffle width as a fraction of the tank radius, w/R (0 \textless{} w/R \ensuremath{\le} 1). Sets the ring-baffle damping (Miles 1958). Liquid: filled with the width ratio of the tank's own ring baffle (oxidizer-tank slosh block). Hybrid: not filled. \emph{If blank:} Not sent; the endpoint returns the baffle width needed for its target damping (the hybrid motor's own slosh block runs the same way).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Baffle Depth d/R} & \texttt{feed\_\allowbreak{}slosh\_\allowbreak{}baffle\_\allowbreak{}depth\_\allowbreak{}ratio} &  &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Baffle depth below the free surface as a fraction of the radius, d/R (\ensuremath{\ge} 0). Sets the ring-baffle damping (Miles 1958). Filled with the depth ratio the run's slosh block used (hybrid: oxidizer\_tank\_slosh; liquid: the tank's own ring baffle). \emph{If blank:} Not sent; the endpoint uses d/R = 0.10 and lists it below the result as a defaulted field.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Architecture} & \texttt{feed\_\allowbreak{}pressurant\_\allowbreak{}mode} &  &  & Regulated \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Pressurisation architecture: regulated or blowdown. /api/pressurant-sizing sizes the pressurant for this architecture; fields of the other mode are ignored. Not filled from the motor result. Options: Regulated; Blowdown.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Pressurant Gas} & \texttt{feed\_\allowbreak{}pressurant\_\allowbreak{}gas} &  &  & Helium \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Pressurant gas: helium or nitrogen. Sets the gas properties of the sizing. Liquid: filled with the pressurant type of the run (feed\_system.pressurization.type) when it is helium or nitrogen. Hybrid: not filled (the N2O tank is self-pressurised, the run has no pressurant gas). Options: Helium; Nitrogen.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Propellant Volume} & \texttt{feed\_\allowbreak{}pressurant\_\allowbreak{}propellant\_\allowbreak{}volume} & m\textsuperscript{3} &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Propellant volume to expel, m\textsuperscript{3} (\textgreater{} 0). Volume the pressurant must displace. Liquid: filled with the propellant volume of the run's oxidizer tank (propellant\_tanks.oxidizer\_tank.propellant\_data.volume\_required, L \ensuremath{\rightarrow} m\textsuperscript{3}, without the ullage) unless you edit it. Hybrid: not filled; the N2O tank is self-pressurised and the run publishes no stored-gas system. \emph{If blank:} The endpoint rejects the request naming this field (required).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Gas Temperature} & \texttt{feed\_\allowbreak{}pressurant\_\allowbreak{}initial\_\allowbreak{}temperature} & K &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Pressurant gas temperature, K (\textgreater{} 0; at the end of the expansion the gas must stay above 4.222 K for helium and 63.151 K for nitrogen). Sets the gas density and the required mass. Not filled from the motor result. \emph{If blank:} The endpoint uses 293.15 K (20 \ensuremath{^\circ}C, an HRMA choice) and lists it below the result as a defaulted field.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Tank Pressure} & \texttt{feed\_\allowbreak{}pressurant\_\allowbreak{}tank\_\allowbreak{}pressure} & bar &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Propellant tank pressure, bar (\textgreater{} 0; the storage pressure must exceed (1 + regulator margin) \ensuremath{\times} this value). The regulated outlet pressure the pressurant must hold. Liquid: filled with the tank pressure of the run (feed\_system.tank\_pressure\_bar; for a pump-fed engine this is the pump-NPSH tank pressure, not the chamber pressure). Hybrid: not filled. Used only in regulated mode. \emph{If blank:} The endpoint rejects the request naming this field (required in regulated mode).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Storage Pressure} & \texttt{feed\_\allowbreak{}pressurant\_\allowbreak{}storage\_\allowbreak{}pressure} & bar &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Pressurant storage bottle pressure, bar (must exceed (1 + regulator margin) \ensuremath{\times} tank pressure). Sets the bottle volume and the gas mass. Not filled from the motor result. Used only in regulated mode. \emph{If blank:} The endpoint uses 200 bar (common industrial bottle) and lists it below the result as a defaulted field.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Regulator Margin [reg]} & \texttt{feed\_\allowbreak{}pressurant\_\allowbreak{}regulator\_\allowbreak{}margin} &  &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Regulator pressure margin, fraction (\textgreater{} 0). The bottle stops feeding below (1 + margin) \ensuremath{\times} tank pressure; the storage pressure must exceed it. Not filled from the motor result. Used only in regulated mode. \emph{If blank:} The endpoint uses 0.10 (an HRMA choice) and lists it below the result as a defaulted field.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Collapse Factor [reg]} & \texttt{feed\_\allowbreak{}pressurant\_\allowbreak{}collapse\_\allowbreak{}factor} &  &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Pressurant collapse factor, \ensuremath{\times} (accepted band 1.0--1.6). Multiplies the gas mass for heat loss to the cold propellant (Sutton Ch. 6); outside the band nothing is sized. Not filled from the motor result. Used only in regulated mode. \emph{If blank:} The endpoint uses 1.0 (no collapse, the optimistic lower bound) and lists it below the result as a defaulted field.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Initial Ullage Vol} & \texttt{feed\_\allowbreak{}pressurant\_\allowbreak{}initial\_\allowbreak{}ullage\_\allowbreak{}volume} & m\textsuperscript{3} &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Initial ullage volume, m\textsuperscript{3} (\textgreater{} 0). Gas volume at the start of blowdown. Liquid: filled with the ullage volume of the run's oxidizer tank (propellant\_data.ullage\_volume, L \ensuremath{\rightarrow} m\textsuperscript{3}). Hybrid: not filled. Used only in blowdown mode. \emph{If blank:} The endpoint rejects the request naming this field (required in blowdown mode).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Initial Pressure} & \texttt{feed\_\allowbreak{}pressurant\_\allowbreak{}initial\_\allowbreak{}pressure} & bar &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Initial tank pressure, bar (\textgreater{} 0). Starting pressure of the blowdown expansion. Not filled from the motor result: a blowdown start pressure is a design choice, and the liquid run's tank pressure is a regulated value. Used only in blowdown mode. \emph{If blank:} The endpoint rejects the request naming this field (required in blowdown mode).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Polytropic n [bd]} & \texttt{feed\_\allowbreak{}pressurant\_\allowbreak{}polytropic\_\allowbreak{}n} &  &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Polytropic exponent n of the ullage gas (accepted band 1.0 up to the \ensuremath{\gamma} of the gas: helium 5/3, nitrogen 7/5). Sets how fast the pressure falls during blowdown (1 = isothermal, \ensuremath{\gamma} = adiabatic). Not filled from the motor result. Used only in blowdown mode. \emph{If blank:} The endpoint uses 1.2 (an HRMA choice) and lists it below the result as a defaulted field.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Line Fluid} & \texttt{feed\_\allowbreak{}water\_\allowbreak{}hammer\_\allowbreak{}fluid} &  &  & Water \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Fluid in the feed line. /api/water-hammer takes its density and bulk modulus (wave speed) from it. Liquid: filled with the fluid of the run's oxidizer line (water\_hammer\_fluid\_key). Hybrid: filled with the oxidizer of the run (N2O). Solid: not filled (a solid motor has no liquid line); the selection stays as you leave it. Options: Water; Nitrous oxide (N2O); RP-1 (kerosene); Liquid oxygen.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Line Length} & \texttt{feed\_\allowbreak{}water\_\allowbreak{}hammer\_\allowbreak{}line\_\allowbreak{}length\_\allowbreak{}m} & m &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Feed line length, m (\textgreater{} 0). Sets the pressure-wave round-trip time 2L/a (sudden vs slow closure). Liquid: filled with the length of the run's oxidizer line. Hybrid: filled only if you gave a feed line length on the hybrid page (chug loop); the hybrid solver sizes no line. Solid: not filled. \emph{If blank:} The endpoint rejects the request naming this field (required).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Line Inner Diameter} & \texttt{feed\_\allowbreak{}water\_\allowbreak{}hammer\_\allowbreak{}line\_\allowbreak{}id\_\allowbreak{}mm} & mm &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Line inner diameter, mm (\textgreater{} 0; the wall must be thinner than the inner radius). Sets the flow velocity and the wave speed. Liquid: filled with the inner diameter of the run's oxidizer line (m \ensuremath{\rightarrow} mm). Hybrid: filled only if you gave a feed line diameter on the hybrid page. Solid: not filled. \emph{If blank:} The endpoint rejects the request naming this field (required).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Wall Thickness} & \texttt{feed\_\allowbreak{}water\_\allowbreak{}hammer\_\allowbreak{}wall\_\allowbreak{}thickness\_\allowbreak{}mm} & mm &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Line wall thickness, mm (\textgreater{} 0 and below the inner radius; at or above it the thin-wall pressure rating breaks down and no verdict is issued). Sets the pipe elasticity (wave speed) and the wall stress check. Not filled from the motor result: no motor computes a feed-line wall thickness. \emph{If blank:} The endpoint rejects the request naming this field (required).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Working Pressure} & \texttt{feed\_\allowbreak{}water\_\allowbreak{}hammer\_\allowbreak{}working\_\allowbreak{}pressure\_\allowbreak{}bar} & bar &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Line working pressure, bar. The surge is added to it for the peak-pressure verdict. Liquid: filled with the inlet pressure of the run's oxidizer line (pump discharge; the pressure the motor's own water-hammer block uses). Hybrid: filled with the injector feed pressure P1 of the run (N2O saturation pressure). Solid: not filled. \emph{If blank:} The endpoint rejects the request naming this field (required).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Working Pressure Reference} & \texttt{feed\_\allowbreak{}water\_\allowbreak{}hammer\_\allowbreak{}working\_\allowbreak{}pressure\_\allowbreak{}reference} &  &  & Not specified (both planes checked) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Reference plane of the working pressure: absolute or gauge. Not specified: both readings are checked; if the verdicts differ the endpoint refuses (400) and you must pick one here. Not filled from the motor result. Options: Not specified (both planes checked); Absolute; Gauge.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Mass Flow} & \texttt{feed\_\allowbreak{}water\_\allowbreak{}hammer\_\allowbreak{}mdot\_\allowbreak{}kg\_\allowbreak{}s} & kg/s &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Line mass flow, kg/s (\textgreater{} 0). Sets the flow velocity that the valve stops. Liquid: filled with the mass flow of the run's oxidizer line; hybrid: with the oxidizer mass flow of the run. Solid: not filled. \emph{If blank:} The endpoint rejects the request (a mass flow or a flow velocity is required).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Valve Closure Time} & \texttt{feed\_\allowbreak{}water\_\allowbreak{}hammer\_\allowbreak{}valve\_\allowbreak{}closure\_\allowbreak{}time\_\allowbreak{}ms} & ms &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Valve closure time, ms (\textgreater{} 0). Compared with the wave round-trip time 2L/a: closure faster than it gives the full Joukowsky surge. Not filled from the motor result (no motor models a closure law). \emph{If blank:} Instantaneous closure is assumed (full surge, the conservative bound) and listed below the result as a defaulted field.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Pipe Material} & \texttt{feed\_\allowbreak{}water\_\allowbreak{}hammer\_\allowbreak{}pipe\_\allowbreak{}material} &  &  & Stainless 304 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Pipe material. Supplies the elastic modulus (wave speed) and the strength for the wall check. Liquid: filled with the structural alloy of the run's oxidizer line (pipe\_materials.structural\_key). Hybrid and solid: not filled; the selection stays as you leave it. Options: Stainless 304; Stainless 316; Steel AISI 4130; Aluminum 6061; Titanium 6Al-4V.} \\ \midrule
\end{longtable}}

\textbf{Configuration name} & \texttt{cmp\_\allowbreak{}name} &  &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Name for the snapshot of the current motor result (max 40 characters). Only a label: it does not enter any calculation. \emph{If blank:} An automatic name config-N is used; an existing name is overwritten.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Design A} & \texttt{cmp\_\allowbreak{}ov\_\allowbreak{}a} &  &  &  \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} First stored snapshot (Design A) of the overlay table. Only selects which saved results are compared; nothing is recalculated. Needs at least two snapshots.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Design B} & \texttt{cmp\_\allowbreak{}ov\_\allowbreak{}b} &  &  &  \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Second stored snapshot (Design B); must differ from Design A. Only selects saved results; nothing is recalculated.} \\ \midrule

\subsection{Panels in the result section}

Some analyses run in their own panel in the result section rather than in the dock.

\begin{table}[htbp]
\centering\small
\caption{Panels in the result section}\label{tab:yanpanel}
\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{3.8cm}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{2.0cm}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{9.8cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Panel} & \textbf{Page} & \textbf{Function} \\
\midrule
Transient Analysis --- $P_c(t)$ / $F(t)$ & Hybrid & Time-stepped internal ballistics by feed mode; export to Excel. \\
Tank Blowdown & Hybrid & Pressure, flow and thrust decay of a self-pressurised tank; true total impulse and burn time. \\
Structural FEA & Hybrid, liquid & Stress field, mesh quality and convergence history on an axisymmetric wall section. \\
Thermal FEA & Hybrid & Wall temperature field by transient conduction; peak wall temperature at the end of a finite burn. Answers a different question from the equilibrium temperature of the main chain. \\
Grain Section FEA & Solid & Plane-strain stress and bore strain; the acceptance criterion is the bore-surface strain. \\
Flight Dynamics --- 6-DOF & All three & Rigid-body flight, Barrowman $C_{N\alpha}$/CP, static margin, rail and wind. Linear small-$\alpha$ aerodynamics ($\alpha < 15°$). \\
Injector Design & Hybrid, liquid & Standalone ``what if'' calculator; after every main calculation it is filled with that design's circuit and does not change the main design. \\
Trajectory Analysis & All three & Point-mass ballistic flight; not 6-DOF. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\toprule
\textbf{Input} & \textbf{Identifier} & \textbf{Unit} & \textbf{Form limit} & \textbf{Form default} \\ \midrule

\textbf{Input} & \textbf{Identifier} & \textbf{Unit} & \textbf{Form limit} & \textbf{Form default} \\ \midrule
