\endfoot
\bottomrule
\endlastfoot
\textbf{Feed Mode} & \texttt{tp\_\allowbreak{}feed\_\allowbreak{}mode} &  &  & N2O Blowdown (self-pressurizing) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} How the oxidizer reaches the injector in this time march. Regulated: the oxidizer mass flow is held at its design value for the whole burn; no tank is modelled, so the fill fraction changes nothing and the tank temperature only enters as the N2O inlet temperature. N2O blowdown: a self-pressurising N2O tank holding the design oxidizer mass drives the flow; as it empties, tank pressure, thrust and Pc fall and the run can end before the design burn time (the end event is marked on the chart). Blowdown is disabled when the main design uses a user-set tank pressure. Choices: Regulated (default) or N2O blowdown. Options: Regulated (constant mass flow); N2O Blowdown (self-pressurizing).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Tank Temperature} & \texttt{tp\_\allowbreak{}tank\_\allowbreak{}temp} & K & 240 -- 309 & 293.15 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Initial N2O tank temperature, in K. In N2O blowdown mode it sets the starting vapour pressure and liquid density from the N2O saturation table, so it drives the flow. In Regulated mode the oxidizer flow is prescribed, so it does not drive the feed; it is still passed to the engine as the N2O inlet temperature, which shifts the curves only slightly. Accepted (blowdown): 240--309 K (saturation table band); a temperature outside the N2O liquid range is rejected in both modes with the reason. \emph{If blank:} Empty: 293.15 K is sent (the solver's default tank temperature).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Liquid Fill Fraction} & \texttt{tp\_\allowbreak{}fill} &  & 0.05 -- 0.98 & 0.85 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Fraction of the tank volume filled with liquid N2O at the start (dimensionless, 0--1); the rest is vapour ullage. Read only in N2O blowdown mode: with the design oxidizer mass fixed it sets the tank volume, and so how fast the tank pressure falls. In Regulated mode it changes no number. Accepted: 0.05--0.98; outside it the blowdown run is rejected with the reason. \emph{If blank:} Empty: 0.85 is sent (the solver's default).} \\ \midrule
\end{longtable}}

{\small
\begin{longtable}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{4.7cm}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{3.5cm}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{1.6cm}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{2.2cm}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{3.3cm}@{}}
\caption{Injector Design panel inputs (hybrid)}\label{tab:y-enj-hib}\\
\toprule
\textbf{Input} & \textbf{Identifier} & \textbf{Unit} & \textbf{Form limit} & \textbf{Form default} \\ \midrule
\endfirsthead
\toprule
\textbf{Input} & \textbf{Identifier} & \textbf{Unit} & \textbf{Form limit} & \textbf{Form default} \\ \midrule
\endhead
\multicolumn{5}{r@{}}{\footnotesize\itshape continued on next page}\\
\endfoot
\bottomrule
\endlastfoot
\textbf{Injector type} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}type} &  &  & Showerhead (default) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Injector element family. Drives the geometry model, the discharge-coefficient basis and the atomisation correlation. Options: Showerhead (default); Pressure-swirl / vortex; Pintle (throttleable); Like-impinging (self); Coaxial (single-fluid: jet + annulus).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{dP / Pc ratio} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}dp} &  &  & 0.2 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Injector pressure drop as a fraction of chamber pressure. Typical 0.15-0.30; below 0.15 chug instability is likely (Sutton \& Biblarz 9th ed. Ch. 8; NASA SP-194 Ch. 5-6).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Oxidizer mdot} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}mdot\_\allowbreak{}ox} & kg/s &  & 2 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Oxidizer mass flow rate through the injector.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Inlet pressure P1} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}pfeed} & bar &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Injector inlet pressure P\_1 (bar, absolute). Filled after a calculation only when the main design uses a user-supplied tank pressure. \emph{If blank:} Empty: self-pressurised N2O takes P\_sat(T\_tank), other oxidizers P\_c\ensuremath{\cdot}(1 + dP/P\_c).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Measured C\_d} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}cd} & - &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Measured discharge coefficient of the orifices. Not applied to swirl elements, whose C\_d follows from their geometry. \emph{If blank:} Empty: C\_d comes from the circuit table (inlet + L/D).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Chamber pressure} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}pc} & bar &  & 20 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Chamber pressure at the design point.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Oxidizer density} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}rho\_\allowbreak{}ox} & kg/m3 &  & 786 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Liquid oxidizer density at injection temperature. N2O at 293 K is about 745-790 kg/m3; LOX about 1141 kg/m3.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Orifice inlet} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}inlet} &  &  & Sharp edge \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Orifice inlet geometry. A radiused inlet (r/d \textgreater{}= 0.15) raises Cd to about 0.90-0.92; a sharp edge gives 0.63-0.84 and can hydraulically flip. Options: Sharp edge; Radiused.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Orifice L/D} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}ld} &  &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Orifice length-to-diameter ratio. It selects the discharge coefficient from the circuit C\_d table (inlet type and L/D) and the hydraulic-flip verdict. \emph{If blank:} Hybrid: empty means the circuit default L/D = 4 is used and no flip verdict is issued.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{inj\_n2o} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}n2o} &  &  & checked \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Self-pressurised nitrous oxide flashes across the orifice. With this enabled the Dyer NHNE two-phase model sets the flow rate and the pressure drop follows from tank temperature.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{N2O tank temperature} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}tox} & K &  & 293 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Nitrous oxide tank temperature. Sets saturation pressure (about 50 bar at 293 K) and therefore the available dP.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Radial flow fraction (0-1)} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}radial\_\allowbreak{}fraction} &  &  & 0.5 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Share of the oxidizer flow sent through the radial tip holes (the rest goes through the annulus). This is the real control for a single-fluid hybrid pintle: TMR = f/(1-f) follows from it, and the spray cone angle follows from TMR. Usual band 0.3-0.7.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Pintle BF target} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}bf} &  &  & 0.58 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Pintle blockage factor target BF = n\ensuremath{\cdot}d/(\ensuremath{\pi}\ensuremath{\cdot}D\_p): it sets the tip-hole count when neither the hole count nor the hole diameter is given. 0.58 is an HRMA choice (no literature value); the source of the 0.3-0.74 band is not verified.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Swirl cone half angle target} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}theta} & deg &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Target spray cone HALF-angle of the swirl elements, met through the Giffen-Muraszew inverse (K -\textgreater{} X -\textgreater{} \ensuremath{\theta}). The solvable envelope is 3.7-71.2 deg: a hybrid design outside it is rejected; the liquid panel clamps it to the envelope with a warning.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Secondary Holes} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}pin\_\allowbreak{}holes} &  &  & Radial Holes \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Holes drilled through the pintle tip wall, in one row around the post. Radial: hole axes along the radius (classic pintle). Tangential: drilled at an angle to the radius (geometry only; the swirl is not modelled). None: no tip holes - the element becomes a plain annular injector. Options: None; Radial Holes; Tangential Holes.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Pintle Tip Diameter D\_p} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}pin\_\allowbreak{}dp} & mm &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Outer diameter of the pintle post at its tip (D\_p) - the surface the tip holes are drilled into. It sets the annular gap, the hole count through the blockage factor and the default skip distance. \emph{If blank:} Empty: sized from the oxidizer flow with the annulus rule t = 0.05\ensuremath{\cdot}D\_p (HRMA choice, no literature value).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Annular Gap t} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}pin\_\allowbreak{}t} & mm &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Radial clearance between the pintle post (D\_p) and the body bore (t) - the annulus the axial oxidizer sheet flows through. If given, it fixes the annulus area and the tip holes take the rest of the flow area. \emph{If blank:} Empty: solved from the annulus flow area.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Tip Hole Count n} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}pin\_\allowbreak{}n} &  &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Number of holes in the single circumferential row on the pintle tip (n). If given with the hole diameter, the two fix the tip-hole flow area. \emph{If blank:} Empty: from the blockage factor BF = n\ensuremath{\cdot}d/(\ensuremath{\pi}\ensuremath{\cdot}D\_p) = 0.58 (HRMA choice).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Tip Hole Diameter d} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}pin\_\allowbreak{}d} & mm &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Diameter of each tip hole (d). Inputs that over-determine the flow (D\_p, t, n and d all given and not matching) are rejected with the flow mismatch. \emph{If blank:} Empty: solved so the holes carry their share of the oxidizer flow area.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Skip Distance L\_s} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}pin\_\allowbreak{}ls} & mm &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Axial distance from the annulus exit (body face) to the axis of the tip-hole row (L\_s; Dressler \& Bauer 2000). Geometry and drawing only - no model uses it. \emph{If blank:} Empty: L\_s = D\_p (HRMA choice, no literature value).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Tangential Hole Angle} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}pin\_\allowbreak{}ang} & deg &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Angle between each hole axis and the local radius (0\ensuremath{^\circ} = radial, 90\ensuremath{^\circ} = tangent). Geometry/CAD only: the tangential momentum and the swirl it induces are NOT modelled; the reported spray angle is the radial value (a lower bound).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Injector Body Outer Diameter} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}pin\_\allowbreak{}od} & mm &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Outer diameter of the injector body (housing) that surrounds the annulus bore. If given, the body wall (OD - bore)/2 is checked and drawn; it must fit inside the chamber. \emph{If blank:} Empty: HRMA does not size the body (it needs housing material, allowable stress and the pressure across the body wall) and draws only the bore D\_p + 2t.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Number of Doublet Pairs} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}imp\_\allowbreak{}pairs} &  &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Number of like-on-like hole pairs (2 holes each). Given alone, the hole diameter is solved from the oxidizer flow; given together with the hole diameter, the two must deliver the target flow within 5\%. \emph{If blank:} Empty: the circuit plans the fewest holes whose diameter falls inside the 0.5-2.5 mm design band, rounded up to an even count.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Hole Diameter d} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}imp\_\allowbreak{}d} & mm &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Diameter of each doublet hole. If given, the pair count is the nearest whole number for this diameter and the published diameter is the one that delivers the target flow exactly with that count; a plan off by more than 5\% is rejected with the nearest valid plans. \emph{If blank:} Empty: the injector circuit sizes it from the oxidizer flow.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Impingement Angle 2\ensuremath{\theta}} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}imp\_\allowbreak{}angle} & deg &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} FULL angle 2\ensuremath{\theta} between the two jets of each doublet. It sets the jet direction (axial velocity component) and the drawn impingement geometry; the hole plan does not depend on it. Must lie strictly between 0\ensuremath{^\circ} and 180\ensuremath{^\circ}; outside 40-90\ensuremath{^\circ} a band note is shown (HRMA heuristic threshold; NASA SP-8089 gives 60\ensuremath{^\circ} as the design value). \emph{If blank:} Empty: 60\ensuremath{^\circ} (declared).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Swirl Chamber Diameter D\_s} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}sw\_\allowbreak{}ds} & mm &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Diameter of the swirl (spin) chamber of each element. With the exit orifice diameter d\_o it fixes the inlet area that gives the atomizer constant K. Below 1.25\ensuremath{\cdot}d\_o the Giffen-Muraszew geometry assumption breaks down and a warning is shown. \emph{If blank:} Empty: D\_s = 2.5\ensuremath{\cdot}d\_o (Lefebvre \& McDonell, typical simplex proportion; declared).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Tangential Slots per Element} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}sw\_\allowbreak{}nslots} &  &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Number of tangential inlet slots in each swirl element; together they carry the element inlet area A\_p = K\ensuremath{\cdot}D\_s\ensuremath{\cdot}d\_o. The element count and the exit orifice come from the injector circuit. \emph{If blank:} Empty: 6 (server default, declared).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Slot Width w} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}sw\_\allowbreak{}w} & mm &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Width of each rectangular tangential slot. Give the width and the height together, or neither. If given, the slots fix the atomizer constant K and with it the spray angle. \emph{If blank:} Empty: the slots are sized from the target spray angle (w = 2h, HRMA proportion).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Slot Height h} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}sw\_\allowbreak{}h} & mm &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Height of each rectangular tangential slot. \emph{If blank:} Give it together with the slot width, or leave both empty.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Number of holes} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}sh\_\allowbreak{}n} &  &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Number of showerhead orifices. \emph{If blank:} Empty: the circuit plans the fewest holes inside the diameter band.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Min Hole Diameter} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}sh\_\allowbreak{}dmin} & mm &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Lower edge of the hole-diameter band the injector circuit plans in. The circuit uses the fewest holes whose diameter falls inside [min, max]; a hole count fixed in Injector Design overrides that search. \emph{If blank:} Empty: 0.5 mm (design band 0.5-2.5 mm, Sutton \& Biblarz 9th ed. p. 337; declared).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Max Hole Diameter} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}sh\_\allowbreak{}dmax} & mm &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Upper edge of the hole-diameter band the injector circuit plans in; it must be larger than the minimum. \emph{If blank:} Empty: 2.5 mm (design band 0.5-2.5 mm, Sutton \& Biblarz 9th ed. p. 337; declared).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Inner Jet Flow Share (0.1-0.9)} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}coax\_\allowbreak{}f} &  &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Share of the oxidizer flow through the inner jet; the rest flows through the outer annulus. In a hybrid BOTH passages carry oxidizer (the fuel is the solid grain). The inner-jet and annulus diameters, the annulus gap and the recess are computed from this share and the oxidizer flow. Values outside 0.1-0.9 are rejected, not clamped. \emph{If blank:} Empty: 0.6 (HRMA choice, no literature value; declared).} \\ \midrule
\end{longtable}}

{\small
\begin{longtable}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{4.7cm}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{3.5cm}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{1.6cm}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{2.2cm}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{3.3cm}@{}}
\caption{Injector Design panel inputs (liquid)}\label{tab:y-enj-sivi}\\
\toprule
\textbf{Input} & \textbf{Identifier} & \textbf{Unit} & \textbf{Form limit} & \textbf{Form default} \\ \midrule
\endfirsthead
\toprule
\textbf{Input} & \textbf{Identifier} & \textbf{Unit} & \textbf{Form limit} & \textbf{Form default} \\ \midrule
\endhead
\multicolumn{5}{r@{}}{\footnotesize\itshape continued on next page}\\
\endfoot
\bottomrule
\endlastfoot
\textbf{Injector type} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}type} &  &  & Unlike doublet (default) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Injector element family. Drives the geometry model, the discharge-coefficient basis and the atomisation correlation. Options: Unlike doublet (default); Unlike triplet (2:1); Like-impinging (self); Showerhead; Pintle (throttleable); Coaxial swirl; Pressure-swirl.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{dP / Pc ratio} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}dp} &  &  & 0.2 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Injector pressure drop as a fraction of chamber pressure. Typical 0.15-0.30; below 0.15 chug instability is likely (Sutton \& Biblarz 9th ed. Ch. 8; NASA SP-194 Ch. 5-6).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Oxidizer mdot} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}mdot\_\allowbreak{}ox} & kg/s &  & 2 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Oxidizer mass flow rate through the injector.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Measured C\_d} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}cd} & - &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Measured discharge coefficient of the orifices, the same quantity as the Discharge Coefficient Cd of the main form. Not applied to swirl elements, whose Cd follows from their geometry. \emph{If blank:} Empty: Cd from the circuit table (inlet + L/D).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Fuel mdot} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}mdot\_\allowbreak{}fuel} & kg/s &  & 0.8 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Fuel mass flow rate (liquid engines only). Set by the mixture ratio: mdot\_fuel = mdot\_ox / (O/F).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Chamber pressure} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}pc} & bar &  & 100 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Chamber pressure at the design point.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Oxidizer density} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}rho\_\allowbreak{}ox} & kg/m3 &  & 1141 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Liquid oxidizer density at injection temperature. N2O at 293 K is about 745-790 kg/m3; LOX about 1141 kg/m3.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Fuel density} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}rho\_\allowbreak{}fuel} & kg/m3 &  & 810 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Liquid fuel density. RP-1 about 810 kg/m3, ethanol about 789 kg/m3.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Orifice inlet} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}inlet} &  &  & Sharp edge \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Orifice inlet geometry. A radiused inlet (r/d \textgreater{}= 0.15) raises Cd to about 0.90-0.92; a sharp edge gives 0.63-0.84 and can hydraulically flip. Options: Sharp edge; Radiused.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Orifice L/D} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}ld} &  &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Orifice length-to-diameter ratio. It selects the discharge coefficient from the circuit C\_d table (inlet type and L/D) and the hydraulic-flip verdict. \emph{If blank:} Hybrid: empty means the circuit default L/D = 4 is used and no flip verdict is issued.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Pintle TMR target} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}tmr} &  &  & 1 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Pintle total momentum ratio target. TMR = 1 gives a 60 deg spray half angle (Cheng 2017); usual band 0.5-2.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Pintle BF target} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}bf} &  &  & 0.58 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Pintle blockage factor target BF = n\ensuremath{\cdot}d/(\ensuremath{\pi}\ensuremath{\cdot}D\_p): it sets the tip-hole count when neither the hole count nor the hole diameter is given. 0.58 is an HRMA choice (no literature value); the source of the 0.3-0.74 band is not verified.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Swirl cone half angle target} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}theta} & deg &  & 45 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Target spray cone HALF-angle of the swirl elements, met through the Giffen-Muraszew inverse (K -\textgreater{} X -\textgreater{} \ensuremath{\theta}). The solvable envelope is 3.7-71.2 deg: a hybrid design outside it is rejected; the liquid panel clamps it to the envelope with a warning.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Number of Injector Elements} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}n\_\allowbreak{}el} &  &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Number of injection elements (count). It fixes the hole count of the injector circuits; the hole diameters then follow from the flow areas. Unlike doublet, showerhead, coaxial: holes per circuit (one fuel + one oxidizer hole per element). Like-on-like doublet: same-fluid PAIRS per circuit (two holes each), 1-60 because the circuit planner allows at most 120 holes per circuit; more is rejected, not clamped. Not used for the pintle (a single element; the field is hidden). Accepted band 1-20000. \emph{If blank:} Empty: each circuit plans the fewest holes inside its 0.5-2.5 mm diameter band and the answer says so.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Pintle Post Diameter D\_p} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}pin\_\allowbreak{}dp} &  &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Outer diameter of the pintle post at its tip (D\_p, mm); the fuel tip holes are drilled into it and the oxidizer flows through the annulus around it. With the annulus area fixed by the oxidizer circuit, D\_p sets the annular gap t, and through the blockage factor the tip-hole count. Must be a finite positive length; the annulus bore D\_p + 2t must fit inside the chamber. \emph{If blank:} Empty: sized from the oxidizer flow with the annulus rule t = 0.05\ensuremath{\cdot}D\_p (HRMA choice, no literature value).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Oxidizer Annular Gap t} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}pin\_\allowbreak{}t} &  &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Radial gap of the oxidizer annulus around the pintle post (t, mm). The annulus area pi\ensuremath{\cdot}(D\_p + t)\ensuremath{\cdot}t must equal the oxidizer circuit flow area: given alone, D\_p is solved from it; given with D\_p, the two must agree within 5\% (HRMA tolerance) or the design is rejected with the mismatch. \emph{If blank:} Empty: solved from the oxidizer flow area.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Fuel Tip Hole Count n} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}pin\_\allowbreak{}n} &  &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Number of radial fuel holes in the single row on the pintle tip (whole number \ensuremath{\ge} 1). The holes carry the fuel circuit flow area n\ensuremath{\cdot}pi\ensuremath{\cdot}d\textsuperscript{2}/4, so the hole diameter follows from n. \emph{If blank:} Empty: from the blockage factor n\ensuremath{\cdot}d/(pi\ensuremath{\cdot}D\_p) = 0.58 (HRMA choice, no literature value).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Fuel Tip Hole Diameter d} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}pin\_\allowbreak{}d} &  &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Diameter of each radial fuel tip hole (d, mm). Given alone, the hole count is the nearest whole number for this diameter and the published diameter is the one that delivers the fuel circuit area exactly with that count; a plan more than 5\% off (also with a given count) is rejected with the nearest valid plans. \emph{If blank:} Empty: solved from the fuel flow area.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Skip Distance L\_s} & \texttt{inj\_\allowbreak{}pin\_\allowbreak{}ls} &  &  & (blank) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Axial distance from the annulus exit (injector face) to the axis of the tip-hole row (L\_s, mm; definition Dressler \& Bauer, AIAA 2000-3871). Geometry and CAD only: no performance model uses it. Must be shorter than the chamber. \emph{If blank:} Empty: L\_s = D\_p (HRMA choice, no literature value).} \\ \midrule
\end{longtable}}

\textbf{Body Diameter} & \texttt{sd\_\allowbreak{}body\_\allowbreak{}d} & m &  & 0.150 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Outer body diameter (m). Sets the reference area \ensuremath{\pi}d\textsuperscript{2}/4 and scales the fin normal force (span/diameter)\textsuperscript{2} in the Barrowman CP. Must be \textgreater{} 0. Filled from the page vehicle definition when the page publishes one. \emph{If blank:} Empty or invalid: the field turns red and Run is blocked.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Total Length} & \texttt{sd\_\allowbreak{}body\_\allowbreak{}l} & m &  & 2 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Total vehicle length from nose tip (m). Must be \textgreater{} 0 and longer than the nose; fin root LE + root chord must fit inside it. Used for the CP/CG diagram and the default fin position. \emph{If blank:} Empty or invalid: the field turns red and Run is blocked.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Nose Length} & \texttt{sd\_\allowbreak{}nose\_\allowbreak{}l} & m &  & 0.4 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Nose cone length (m). The nose CP sits at (nose-type factor \ensuremath{\times} this length) from the tip. Must be \textgreater{} 0 and shorter than the total length. \emph{If blank:} Empty or invalid: the field turns red and Run is blocked.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Nose Type} & \texttt{sd\_\allowbreak{}nose\_\allowbreak{}type} &  &  & Ogive \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Nose shape. Only changes the nose CP factor: ogive 0.466, conical 2/3, parabolic 0.5 (\ensuremath{\times} nose length); the nose normal-force slope stays CN\_\ensuremath{\alpha} = 2. Options: Ogive; Conical; Parabolic.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Fin Count} & \texttt{sd\_\allowbreak{}fin\_\allowbreak{}count} &  &  & 4 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Number of fins, 3 or 4. Multiplies the fin normal-force term of the Barrowman CN\_\ensuremath{\alpha}, so it moves the CP and the static margin. Options: 3; 4.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Fin Root Chord} & \texttt{sd\_\allowbreak{}fin\_\allowbreak{}root} & m &  & 0.2 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Fin root chord (m), the chord along the body. Enters the fin CN\_\ensuremath{\alpha} and fin CP. Must be \textgreater{} 0; root LE + root chord must not exceed the total length. \emph{If blank:} Empty or invalid: the field turns red and Run is blocked.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Fin Tip Chord} & \texttt{sd\_\allowbreak{}fin\_\allowbreak{}tip} & m &  & 0.1 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Fin tip chord (m). Enters the fin CN\_\ensuremath{\alpha} and fin CP; 0 means a pointed (triangular) fin. Must be \ensuremath{\ge} 0. \emph{If blank:} Empty or invalid: the field turns red and Run is blocked.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Fin Span} & \texttt{sd\_\allowbreak{}fin\_\allowbreak{}span} & m &  & 0.11 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Fin span (m), from the body surface to the fin tip. The fin normal force grows with (span/diameter)\textsuperscript{2}. Must be \textgreater{} 0. \emph{If blank:} Empty or invalid: the field turns red and Run is blocked.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Fin Sweep} & \texttt{sd\_\allowbreak{}fin\_\allowbreak{}sweep} & m &  & 0.08 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Fin leading-edge sweep length (m): axial distance from the root LE to the tip LE. Moves the fin CP aft. Must be \ensuremath{\ge} 0. \emph{If blank:} Empty or invalid: the field turns red and Run is blocked.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Fin Root LE from Nose} & \texttt{sd\_\allowbreak{}fin\_\allowbreak{}pos} & m &  & 1.8 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Distance from the nose tip to the fin root leading edge (m). Places the fin CP. Must be \ensuremath{\ge} 0 and (this + root chord) \ensuremath{\le} total length. \emph{If blank:} Empty or invalid: the field turns red and Run is blocked.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Dry Mass} & \texttt{sd\_\allowbreak{}dry\_\allowbreak{}m} & kg &  & 25.00 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Vehicle mass without propellant (kg), sent as dry\_mass. Must be \textgreater{} 0. Read-only in component mode (sum of non-propellant rows). Filled from the page vehicle definition when the page publishes one. \emph{If blank:} Empty or invalid: the field turns red and Run is blocked.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Propellant Mass} & \texttt{sd\_\allowbreak{}prop\_\allowbreak{}m} & kg &  & 4 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Propellant mass burned during the flight (kg), sent as propellant\_mass. Must be \textgreater{} 0. When the page calculation supplies the motor it is overwritten with that motor's propellant mass; read-only in component mode (sum of propellant rows). \emph{If blank:} Empty or invalid: the field turns red and Run is blocked.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Cd\textsubscript{0} (subsonic)} & \texttt{sd\_\allowbreak{}cd0} &  &  & 0.50 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Zero-lift (subsonic) drag coefficient, dimensionless, on the reference area \ensuremath{\pi}d\textsuperscript{2}/4. Must be \textgreater{} 0 here; the endpoint accepts at most 5. Filled from the page vehicle definition when the page publishes one. \emph{If blank:} Empty or invalid: the field turns red and Run is blocked.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Wind Speed} & \texttt{sd\_\allowbreak{}wind} & m/s &  & 5 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Horizontal wind speed (m/s), added to the airflow seen by the vehicle (drives weathercocking). Must be \ensuremath{\ge} 0; the endpoint rejects speeds above the ISA sea-level speed of sound. \emph{If blank:} Empty or invalid: the field turns red and Run is blocked.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Wind From} & \texttt{sd\_\allowbreak{}wind\_\allowbreak{}dir} & \ensuremath{^\circ} from N &  & 0 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Compass bearing the wind blows FROM (degrees from north). The endpoint accepts 0--360. \emph{If blank:} Empty or invalid: the field turns red and Run is blocked.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Launch Elevation} & \texttt{sd\_\allowbreak{}elev} & \ensuremath{^\circ} &  & 90 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Launch rail elevation above the horizon (degrees); 90 is straight up. Must be \textgreater{} 0; the endpoint accepts at most 90. \emph{If blank:} Empty or invalid: the field turns red and Run is blocked.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Launch Azimuth} & \texttt{sd\_\allowbreak{}azimuth} & \ensuremath{^\circ} from N &  & 0 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Launch azimuth (degrees from north): the horizontal direction the rail points. Any finite number. \emph{If blank:} Empty or invalid: the field turns red and Run is blocked.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Rail Length} & \texttt{sd\_\allowbreak{}rail} & m &  & 5 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Launch rail length (m). Attitude is locked while the vehicle is on the rail; the result badge shows the rail length the solver used. Must be \textgreater{} 0. \emph{If blank:} Empty or invalid: the field turns red and Run is blocked.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Thrust} & \texttt{sd\_\allowbreak{}thrust} & N &  & 1200 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Constant thrust (N), used only when no thrust curve is used (no imported motor file and the computed-curve box is off or unavailable). When the page calculation supplies the motor it is overwritten with that value. Must be \textgreater{} 0 when used.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Burn Time} & \texttt{sd\_\allowbreak{}burn} & s &  & 6 \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Burn time (s) of the constant-thrust case, used together with Thrust only when no thrust curve is used. When the page calculation supplies the motor it is overwritten with that value. Must be \textgreater{} 0 when used.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{sd\_use\_curve} & \texttt{sd\_\allowbreak{}use\_\allowbreak{}curve} &  &  & checked \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} On (default): the run flies the thrust curve (or thrust and burn time) of the page calculation, and the Thrust/Burn Time/Propellant Mass fields are filled from it. Off: the form's constant Thrust and Burn Time are used. An imported motor file overrides both.} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Thrust source} & \texttt{sd\_\allowbreak{}thrust\_\allowbreak{}src} &  &  & Page result / form values (default) \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Where thrust comes from. Default: the page calculation (or the form values). Imported: a RASP .eng / RockSim .rse file is parsed by /api/import/motor-file and its thrust curve is flown; if the file holds several motors, the list next to it picks one. Its propellant mass, if given, is written to Propellant Mass for review. Options: Page result / form values (default); Imported motor file (.eng/.rse).} \\ \midrule
\textbf{Thrust source} & \texttt{sd\_\allowbreak{}motor\_\allowbreak{}select} &  &  &  \\*
\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Where thrust comes from. Default: the page calculation (or the form values). Imported: a RASP .eng / RockSim .rse file is parsed by /api/import/motor-file and its thrust curve is flown; if the file holds several motors, the list next to it picks one. Its propellant mass, if given, is written to Propellant Mass for review.} \\ \midrule
\end{longtable}}

\subsection{Analysis Center}

The Analysis Center arranges the same analyses by component: the component tree
(component $\times$ analysis) on the left, the run card in the middle, the
result viewer on the right, and the session's run history at the bottom.
Components: chamber and nozzle wall, nozzle internal flow, chamber acoustics,
solid grain section, tank / bolted joint / line. \ui{Reload from current result}
refills the run card's inputs from the last calculation. A result opened from
the history is a stored result and says so in its title.

\ekran{img/v3_0_5/hibrit_analiz_merkezi_en.png}{Analysis Center: component
tree, run card and result viewer.}{fig:merkez}

\ekran{img/v3_0_5/hibrit_analiz_merkezi_akustik_en.png}{Analysis Center: an
acoustic-mode table run.}{fig:merkez-akustik}

\ui{READY} & The analysis can be run for this motor. \\
\ui{AWAITING RESULT} & No calculation on the page yet; calculate the motor first. \\
\ui{NOT APPLICABLE} & The analysis does not apply to this motor type; the reason is on the row (example: combustion stability in a solid motor, which has no injector and no feed system). The row is not hidden. \\
\ui{NOT IN CENTER} & The analysis runs in its own panel. \\
\ui{NO VERDICT DECLARED} & The analysis publishes no acceptance verdict; read the numbers and the list of items not modelled. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\begin{table}[htbp]
\centering\small
\caption{Verdicts of the analyses in the Center}\label{tab:merkez-analiz}
\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{4.2cm}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{11.4cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Analysis} & \textbf{Verdict and reading} \\
\midrule
Structural (linear static, axisymmetric) & Minimum of the safety-factor field; read with its scope, the governing mechanism (\kod{binding}) and mesh convergence. On an unconverged mesh the number is a trend. \\
CFD (Euler, shock capturing, $p_w$ separation verdict) & The convergence verdict has three states: \ui{CONVERGED}, \ui{NOT CONVERGED}, verdict not published. Only a firm safe verdict is green. The \ui{INVISCID (Euler)} badge says there is no wall shear and no wall heat flux. Mass and energy imbalance numbers have no threshold. Compare the wall pressure with the distribution of the Nozzle Flow panel. \\
Acoustic mode table & Chamber mode map and damping budget per mode. This path issues no stability verdict; terms not modelled in the budget are listed separately. \\
Combustion stability (feed-coupled chug loop) & Neutral curve, operating point, growth rate. Without a feed-line length the loop runs without inertance and the badge says so. Measured example (25~kN LOX/RP-1, 60~bar, O/F 2.2): without a line length ``unstable'', 77.4 Hz; with a 2.5~m line ``stable'', 33.6 Hz. A half-filled line group is not sent. \\
Plane strain (SP-8073 acceptance) & Solid only; the acceptance criterion is the bore-surface strain, margin = capacity / peak bore strain. A chamber pressure outside the solid band is rejected. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\section{Launch Site}\label{sec:saha}

\subsection{Purpose}

Selects a launch point on Earth and flies a motor's vehicle from that site,
showing the solved flight path (6-DOF) on a 3D globe.

\subsection{Screen}

\ekran{img/v3_0_5/firlatma_sahasi_acilis_en.png}{Launch Site: globe,
\ui{SELECTED SITE}, \ui{VEHICLE TO FLY} and \ui{FLIGHT PATH} panels.}{fig:saha}

\subsection{Procedure}

\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=1.6em]
  \item Pick the site by clicking the globe or by typing \ui{LATITUDE} and
  \ui{LONGITUDE} and pressing \ui{Apply}.
  \item Choose the \ui{SOURCE}: \ui{Last motor calculated}, \ui{Saved project
  (.hrma)} or \ui{Example vehicle}. With a saved project the vehicle is built
  with the same calculation as the project's page.
  \item Press \ui{Resolve site}, then \ui{Fly this site}.
  \item Play the flight with the time bar; \ui{LIVE READOUT} gives altitude,
  speed and downrange at the selected time, \ui{FLIGHT SUMMARY} the apogee and
  the downrange at the end of the solution.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{Inputs}

\ui{AIRFRAME DRY} excludes the \ui{FLYING INERT MASS}; the page adds the two and sends the sum as \kod{dry\_\allowbreak{}mass}.
A missing vehicle input is rejected by name, or the default used is listed
under \kod{defaults\_\allowbreak{}applied}.

\multicolumn{5}{@{}p{\dimexpr\linewidth\relax}@{}}{\footnotesize \emph{Effect on the calculation:} Fin span (m), sent as fin\_span; must be \ensuremath{\ge} 0. \emph{If blank:} Empty or not a number: not sent -- the solver applies its own declared default and names it under the result.} \\ \midrule

\subsection{Limits}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em]
  \item Earth rotation and the Coriolis effect are not modelled; the ground
  track is a flat-Earth projection.
  \item The path is a suborbital, ballistic flight; the vehicle does not enter
  orbit.
  \item \ui{Exaggerate altitude} is for readability only and is off by default
  (the scale is true).
  \item The 3D globe requires WebGL; without it the screen says \ui{The 3D globe
  could not be started (WebGL required).}
  \item Online satellite tiles (NASA GIBS) and weather data (Open-Meteo) are off
  by default; when enabled, only this page goes online. \ui{Clear map cache}
  deletes the downloaded tiles.
\end{itemize}

% =====================================================================
\section{Formulas Page}\label{sec:formuller}

The Formulas page gives the relations used by the solvers and their sources in
fourteen sections: basic performance parameters, nozzle design, combustion
analysis, solid motors, liquid engines, hybrid motors, heat transfer,
structural analysis, trajectory analysis, safety analysis, manufacturing
analysis, cost analysis, advanced analysis, and the relations behind the
advanced-analysis figures (Bartz 1957, NASA SP-8124, NASA SP-125, NACA Report
1135 and others). Equation numbers follow the source book (example: Sections 1.1
and 1.2, Sutton and Biblarz). If the maths typesetting layer fails to load,
raw markup appears; reload the page.

\ekran{img/v3_0_5/formuller_sayfasi_en.png}{Formulas page: section list.}{fig:formul}

\ekran{img/v3_0_5/formuller_isp_en.png}{Formulas, Section 1.1: the specific
impulse relation and the definition of $c^*$.}{fig:formul-isp}

\subsection{Export gates}

The export section of the hybrid page is in Figure~\ref{fig:hib-disa}.

\ekran{img/v3_0_5/sivi_tasarim_ciktilari_en.png}{The \ui{Design Exports}
section of the liquid page.}{fig:sivi-cikti}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em]
  \item If the geometry is incomplete or a gate is closed no file is produced;
  the rejection names the missing field, the reason and the value sent. No
  partial model is drawn.
  \item If the injector plate thickness has not been earned, the STEP and STL
  packages do not contain the injector part; the package content matches the
  file list in the archive.
  \item The two-layer liquid wall is drawn as two bodies of two materials; the
  cooling channels are not drawn and the drawing note says so.
  \item Star and finocyl grains are not exported to CAD. The tangential pintle
  mode is rejected in CAD.
  \item The assembly STL is not a closed solid; use STEP for CAD work.
  \item The \kod{.eng} header lines carry the status and source of the
  two-phase correction; if the solver published no status, ``not published by
  the solver'' is written.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Safety section of the PDF report}

The technical PDF carries a safety assessment: explosive, toxic and fire
hazards, protective equipment, emergency response and operational safety items.
A provenance line states from which field each input was resolved. Without a
usable chamber pressure, propellant mass, chamber diameter or wall thickness no
safety verdict is produced. Regulatory compliance (NFPA, OSHA, DOT and local
requirements) is not assessed.

\ui{MOTOR DESIGN RISK}, \ui{FACILITY / SITING HAZARD}: LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH / CRITICAL & The two separate verdicts of the Comprehensive Safety panel: the motor's own risk and the facility hazard of the propellant on site. If an axis cannot be evaluated the level is partial and no acceptability verdict is given. & Complete the input of the missing axis; use the facility hazard for siting and distance decisions. \\
Nozzle regime: \ui{PERFECT EXPANSION}, \ui{UNDEREXPANDED}, \ui{OVEREXPANDED}, \ui{SEPARATED}, \ui{NORMAL SHOCK IN NOZZLE}, \ui{UNCHOKED} & Flow regime of the Nozzle Flow panel. & Underexpanded: thrust can be gained with a longer nozzle; overexpanded or separated: reduce the expansion ratio. \\
\ui{CONVERGED}, \ui{NOT CONVERGED}, verdict not published & CFD convergence verdict (Table~\ref{tab:merkez-analiz}). & \\
\end{longtable}

\section{Input Rules and Error Messages}\label{sec:girdikural}

\subsection{Rules}

\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=1.6em]
  \item \textbf{A blank field is not sent.} An optional field left blank is not
  put in the request; the server applies its canonical default and declares it.
  \item \textbf{An out-of-band value is not clipped.} On the solid and liquid
  pages every band is a gate: the request is rejected with
  \kod{input\_\allowbreak{}not\_\allowbreak{}accepted} and the response gives the field, the value, the
  accepted range and the unit. On the hybrid page, fields with a form gate are
  rejected; for fields without a gate the request runs, the value is ignored
  and declared in the warning list with the field name, the value and the band.
  \item \textbf{A computed field is not an input.} For example the hybrid
  oxidizer mass flow is a result of the calculation; putting it in the request
  gets the request rejected.
  \item \textbf{A number-like string is not a number.} A quoted value such as
  \kod{"20.0"}, a non-finite value and a boolean are rejected, each with its own
  reason code.
  \item \textbf{Conflicting inputs are not resolved.} Without a rule that picks
  the winner, the request is rejected and the conflict is named.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{Messages of the hybrid form}

\begin{table}[htbp]
\centering\small
\caption{Browser check messages of the hybrid form}\label{tab:formileti}
\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{8.0cm}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{7.6cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Message} & \textbf{Meaning} \\
\midrule
\ui{Thrust must be positive}; \ui{Burn time must be positive}; \ui{O/F ratio must be positive}; \ui{Chamber pressure must be positive} & Zero or negative value. \\
\ui{Burn time too long (max 300 seconds)} & Upper limit of the form. \\
\ui{O/F ratio too high (max 20)} & Upper limit of the form. \\
\ui{Chamber pressure too high (max 200 bar)} & Upper limit of the form. \\
\ui{Chamber diameter too small (min 10mm)}; \ui{Chamber diameter too large (max 1000mm)} & Limits of the form (the server accepts 10--5000~mm; a chamber wider than 1000~mm is sized by leaving the diameter blank or through the contraction ratio). \\
\ui{Tank pressure (\ldots{} bar) must be higher than chamber pressure (\ldots{} bar). Minimum required: \ldots{} bar} & Lower limit in user tank-pressure mode. \\
\ui{For finite area combustion, fill only ONE parameter} & Contraction ratio or chamber mass flux, not both. \\
\ui{\ldots{} is below (above) the minimum (maximum) this form declares on screen \ldots{} The request was not sent.} & The limit written in the field's label or note is applied. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\subsection{Server rejections}

A calculation rejected by the server (HTTP 422) is shown in the interface
language; the field is named by its screen label and the machine code stays in
the tooltip. Common rejections:
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em]
  \item \textbf{The endpoint does not read this field.} If the endpoint never
  reads the field sent, the request is rejected; silently dropping the field
  would publish the result under a wrong label.
  \item \textbf{No sweep range.} In a parametric sweep with an empty start or
  end, no point is computed.
  \item \textbf{Unknown propellant.} Without a record for the requested
  propellant the request is rejected and the valid names are listed.
  \item \textbf{Missing flow input.} The required fields of the Nozzle Flow
  analysis are not assumed; the rejection code is
  \kod{incomplete\_\allowbreak{}flow\_\allowbreak{}input}.
\end{itemize}

\ekran{img/v3_0_5/kati_ret_422_yogunluk_en.png}{A named rejection (top right) and the
marked field: density 4000~kg/m\textsuperscript{3}, accepted range
500--3000~kg/m\textsuperscript{3}; no design is published.}{fig:ret422}

On a JavaScript error or a network interruption the application shows a box
titled \ui{ERROR DETECTED}: source (network, form validation, data parsing,
JavaScript), time, context and the original message. If a server response is
not valid JSON nothing is drawn and the raw body is written to the browser
console.

\section{Scope and Limits}\label{sec:kapsam}

\subsection{Model level}

The models are closed-form and one-dimensional relations. Turbopump maps,
cavitation, rotordynamics, bearing life, start-up and shut-down transients and
two- and three-dimensional conjugate heat transfer are not included. The nozzle
CFD panel is two-dimensional: it solves the Euler equations with shock
capturing and has an optional viscous mode; it is not a validated viscous
design tool.

\subsection{Measured deviations}

Measured relative errors against the shipped experimental database (current
numbers in \kod{docs/\allowbreak{}VALIDATION\_\allowbreak{}STATUS.md}):

\begin{table}[htbp]
\centering\small
\caption{Median relative error measured against the experimental database}\label{tab:sapma}
\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{2.2cm}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{4.4cm}cc>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5.4cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Motor} & \textbf{Quantity} & \textbf{N} & \textbf{Median error} & \textbf{Note} \\
\midrule
Liquid & Vacuum Isp & 14 & 1.0\,\% & Published engine data \\
Liquid & Vacuum thrust & 4 & 0.2\,\% & 4/4 weak evidence \\
Liquid & Sea-level Isp & 4 & 2.0\,\% & Small sample \\
Solid & Burn rate & 27 & 0.5\,\% & 27/27 own fit data \\
Hybrid & Characteristic velocity & 18 & 3.3\,\% & \\
Hybrid & Specific impulse & 18 & 5.0\,\% & \\
Hybrid & Final port diameter & 18 & 10.1\,\% & \\
Hybrid & Chamber pressure & 35 & 10.9\,\% & \\
Hybrid & Regression rate & 35 & 36.7\,\% & 17/35 own fit data \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

The 1\,\% median error on the liquid side shows that Isp is reproduced when
the true operating point and the published geometry are given; it does not show
that the flight performance of an unknown motor is predicted with this error.
Rows marked ``own fit data'' are scored against the data the coefficients were
derived from; they are not independent validation. The scatter of the hybrid
regression rate is a known property of hybrid motors.

\subsection{Verdicts not published}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em]
  \item The CFD convergence verdict for runs outside the scope of the
  self-consistency gate.
  \item A stability verdict on the acoustic-mode path.
  \item A verified two-phase correction in the solid motor.
  \item Buckling without a declared external-pressure load case.
  \item Tungsten nozzle erosion (no published coefficient band).
  \item Jacket flow and pressure drop of dump cooling.
  \item Ablative liner thickness without net heating, and when the recession
  rate exceeds the validity ceiling of the Level-1 Q* model (0.35~mm/s).
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Known limitations (3.0.5)}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em]
  \item The liquid delivered Isp is a preliminary-design estimate; the losses of
  a real injector and chamber are determined by test.
  \item For solid motors below about 75~mm the delivered Isp can be optimistic.
  \item Heat transfer is a Bartz-level estimate; a burn-through margin needs
  thermocouple data.
  \item Combustion instability, ignition transients and hard starts are outside
  the model; the delivered $c^*$ efficiency is determined by static firing.
  \item Two-layer regenerative wall: low-cycle fatigue, creep, the thermal
  mismatch between liner and shell, bond strength and buckling are not modelled; the throat
  axial membrane check is not repeated on the closeout; the staged-cycle
  preburner pressure ladder is not in the jacket pressure budget.
  \item RP-1 carbon deposits are modelled only inside the NASA TP-2862 envelope.
  \item Hybrid with user tank pressure: regulator lock-up and thermal drift are
  not modelled, the tank structural mass is not computed.
  \item CEA comparison: solid propellants of uncertain composition show no
  number; the black-powder card has low confidence; the sea-level Isp of a
  separated liquid nozzle is RocketCEA's estimate.
  \item The coaxial hybrid element publishes no atomisation number.
  \item In a back-pressured 2D CFD run, shocked overexpanded cases may show
  backflow at the exit; these cases return with ``not converged / plateau'' and
  a \kod{suspect} separation verdict. Treat the exit-region wall pressure and
  separation output as qualitative.
  \item In the API and the PDF report the hybrid TNT equivalent is applied to
  the total propellant mass (conservatively high); the safety panel does not
  evaluate the TNT equivalent for hybrids.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Not in this version}

A C++ solver core; 3D CFD, 3D FEA, reacting CFD, modal FEA; detailed CAD
(injector head and dome, flanges, bolt circle, O-ring grooves, regenerative
channels, closed STL); turbopump, preburner, feed-line, valve and gimbal models
and their CAD; exhaust plume visuals. The turbopump power balance on the cycle
card is a cycle calculation, not a pump design.

\subsection{Flight worthiness}

\begin{uyarikutu}
\small\color{hrmadark}
HRMA is a preliminary design and analysis tool. The final design, safety
decision and qualification of a motor that will fly require fatigue and creep
analysis, physical testing (static firing) and a formal verification process.
Every critical result is confirmed by physical testing.
\end{uyarikutu}

\section{Glossary}\label{sec:ekb}

\begin{description}[leftmargin=0pt, labelindent=0pt, style=unboxed, itemsep=2pt]
  \item[Ablative.] Protective material that carries heat away by controlled recession of its surface.
  \item[Blowdown.] Emptying of a tank under its own pressure; the feed pressure falls during the burn.
  \item[Characteristic length, L*.] Ratio of chamber volume to throat area.
  \item[Characteristic velocity, $c^*$.] Measure of combustion-chamber performance; independent of the nozzle: $c^* = P_c\,A_t/\dot m$.
  \item[Chug.] Low-frequency pressure oscillation between the feed system and the chamber.
  \item[Coking.] Carbon left on a hot wall by a hydrocarbon coolant.
  \item[Contraction ratio.] Ratio of chamber cross-section to throat area.
  \item[Divergence loss.] Thrust loss from the non-axial component of the exit velocity.
  \item[Expansion ratio.] Ratio of nozzle exit area to throat area.
  \item[Fail-closed.] The behaviour of showing a reason instead of a value when a result cannot be computed.
  \item[Fuel grain.] The shaped body of a solid or hybrid fuel.
  \item[Kn.] Ratio of burning surface to throat area (solid motor).
  \item[Nozzle.] Converging-diverging duct that accelerates the combustion products.
  \item[O/F.] Ratio of oxidizer mass flow to fuel mass flow.
  \item[Port.] The flow channel inside a fuel grain.
  \item[Provenance line.] A line stating the source of a published number.
  \item[Regenerative cooling.] Cooling by passing a propellant through channels in the chamber wall.
  \item[Regression rate.] Recession rate of the fuel surface in a hybrid motor; mm/s.
  \item[Regulated design point.] Hybrid design point with the oxidizer flow taken as constant through the burn.
  \item[Safety factor.] Ratio of strength to applied stress.
  \item[Self-pressurised.] Feeding of an oxidizer (N\textsubscript{2}O) by its own vapour pressure.
  \item[Slosh.] Free-surface oscillation of the liquid in a tank.
  \item[Spallation.] Detachment of the carbon deposit on a hot wall; the wall underneath sees the deposit-free heat flux.
  \item[Specific impulse, Isp.] Impulse per unit weight of propellant; s. The basis of a published value (design point, sea level, vacuum) is stated on its label.
  \item[Thrust coefficient, $C_F$.] Dimensionless measure of the nozzle's contribution; $F = C_F\,P_c\,A_t$.
  \item[Throat.] Smallest cross-section of the nozzle; the station where the flow reaches the speed of sound.
  \item[Total impulse.] Integral of thrust over the burn; N·s.
  \item[Water hammer.] Pressure surge in a line caused by a sudden change of flow.
  \item[Web.] Thickness between the burning surface and the outer boundary of a grain.
\end{description}

\section{Canonical Bands and Design Check Bands}\label{sec:eke}

\subsection{Canonical bands}

The canonical envelope kept by the endpoint layer in SI units
(\kod{CANONICAL\_\allowbreak{}LIMITS}). The form layer's bands in user units (mm, bar) are
derived from it.

\begin{table}[htbp]
\centering\small
\caption{Canonical bands}\label{tab:kanonik}
\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5.2cm}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{4.4cm}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{4.4cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Quantity} & \textbf{Canonical band} & \textbf{Unit} \\
\midrule
Thrust & 10 -- 1\,000\,000 & N \\
Chamber pressure & 1 -- 500 & bar \\
Tank pressure & 5 -- 700 & bar \\
Burn time & 0.1 -- 300 & s \\
Chamber diameter & 0.01 -- 5.0 & m \\
Chamber length & 0.05 -- 20.0 & m \\
Throat diameter & 0.001 -- 2.0 & m \\
Exit diameter & 0.002 -- 5.0 & m \\
Port diameter & 0.005 -- 1.0 & m \\
Fuel-grain length & 0.05 -- 10.0 & m \\
Web thickness & 0.001 -- 0.5 & m \\
O/F and mixture ratio & 0.5 -- 20.0 & -- \\
Chamber temperature & 200 -- 5000 & K \\
Ambient temperature & 180 -- 340 & K \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

No band is defined for fields without a product-wide measured envelope
(oxidizer temperature, stoichiometric O/F, initial and final mass, drag
coefficient, reference area); the value must be finite and positive.

\subsection{Hybrid design check bands}

The bands below do not reject the calculation; a value outside them is named in
the warning list. The bands come from \kod{validation\_\allowbreak{}system.py}.

\begin{table}[htbp]
\centering\small
\caption{Hybrid design check bands}\label{tab:tasarimbant}
\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{6.0cm}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{4.0cm}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5.6cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Criterion} & \textbf{Expected range} & \textbf{Note} \\
\midrule
Isp, N\textsubscript{2}O/HTPB; N\textsubscript{2}O/paraffin; LOX/HTPB & 180--250; 190--260; 220--280~s & Critical below 80\,\% of the lower end or above 120\,\% of the upper end, warning in between. \\
O/F, N\textsubscript{2}O/HTPB and N\textsubscript{2}O/paraffin & 4.0--12.0 & \\
$c^*$, N\textsubscript{2}O/HTPB; N\textsubscript{2}O/paraffin & 1350--1650; 1400--1700~m/s & \\
Chamber pressure & 5--100~bar & \\
$\gamma$ & 1.10--1.35 & \\
Injector Reynolds number & 1000--200\,000 & \\
Injector $\Delta P/P_c$ & 0.15--0.35 & Lower limit chug stability, upper limit feed-system cost. \\
Injector exit velocity & 10--100~m/s & \\
Initial port diameter & 5--100~mm & \\
Final port diameter & 10--200~mm & \\
Chamber length & 50--2000~mm & \\
Expansion ratio & no fixed band & The verdict is read from the run's own separation screen (Summerfield criterion); supersonic exit requires $\varepsilon > 1$. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}
